# Tapir

> Tapir is a free, open-source (MIT) add-on for Graphisoft Archicad 25–30, by
> ENZYME-APD and its community. It adds 641 JSON commands to Archicad's own JSON API, a palette
> that runs Python scripts in one click, a Grasshopper plugin (package `tapir` on the Rhino Package
> Manager) and MCP servers so AI assistants can drive Archicad. A new release ships every Monday.

- Site: https://archicad-api.com/
- Source, issues and releases: https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation
- Download (Tapir Installer for Windows and macOS): https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest
- Community (Discord): https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY
- Tapir started in 2022 as R&D at Enzyme, an architecture practice; the add-on is built on Tibor
  Lorántfy's archicad-additional-json-commands template.

## How a Tapir command is sent

Archicad (with a project open) answers JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:19723`. Tapir's commands go
through Archicad's own `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`, in the namespace `TapirCommand`:

```json
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {"addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetAddOnVersion"},
                "addOnCommandParameters": {}}}
```

The answer is `{"succeeded": true, "result": {"addOnCommandResponse": {...}}}`. Python's standard
library is enough (`urllib.request`); the official `archicad` package and the Tapir Grasshopper
plugin send the same JSON. Every command, with its parameters and an example, is in
[commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md) and [commands.json](https://archicad-api.com/commands.json).

Automation for Archicad

## Archicad, on *autopilot.*

Number every door along a line. Colour the model by any property. Check a project before it goes out. Tapir adds hundreds of commands to Archicad and a palette that runs scripts in one click.

[Download WINDOWS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Win.exe) [Download MACOS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Mac.zip)

100% freeOpen source (MIT)[Watch the tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/)[All downloads](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest)

Automatic Numbering Based on Polyline · 6 doors numbered D01–D06

Mon [A new release every week](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases)

### Start where you *already work.*

Two of the three need no programming. All of them use the same commands.

For architects

#### Scripts in the palette

Open the Tapir palette, pick a script and press Run Script. The built-in scripts are there from the start, and more are shared by the community.

[Browse scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/)

For computational designers

#### Grasshopper

The tapir package in Rhino's Package Manager. Walls, doors, windows and more as components that read and change the model, with the names of Archicad's settings dialogs.

[Grasshopper guide](https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/)

For developers

#### Python and the JSON API

Every command answers on port 19723, each with a schema and an example. Python's standard library is enough.

[Command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/)

### Six jobs it *already does.*

Five built-in scripts of the Tapir palette and one workflow script, each a short Python file you can read and change.

-  Built-in script

#### Number elements along a line

Select a polyline and the doors, zones or objects to number. Each one gets its Element ID in the order the polyline passes it.

Changes the model `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`

[Automatic Numbering Based on Polyline](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline.py)
-  Built-in script

#### Colour the model by a property

Pick a property; every element gets a colour for its value, with a legend of the values and how many elements have each. Number values can be grouped into ranges.

Read only `HighlightElements`

[Property Highlighter](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyHighlighter.py)
-  Built-in script

#### Check a project before it goes out

Lists elements without an ID, zones with the same number, unclassified and duplicate elements, empty stories and unused layers. Export the list to Excel or turn it into Issues.

Read only `GetClassificationsOfElements`

[Project Health Check](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ProjectHealthCheck.py)
-  Built-in script

#### Publish on a schedule

Publishes the chosen Publisher Sets now or on a schedule, every few hours or daily at a set time. It can receive the Teamwork changes and update the drawings first, and logs every run.

Writes files `PublishPublisherSet`

[Batch Publisher](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BatchPublisher.py)
-  Built-in script

#### Tidy up the View Map

Finds the views that are neither placed on a layout nor published, and moves the ones you choose into a separate folder that keeps their folder structure.

Changes the model `API.MoveNavigatorItem`

[Unused View Cleaner](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/UnusedViewCleaner.py)
-  Workflow

#### Export the model to OBJ

Writes the 3D model, or only the selected elements, to a Wavefront OBJ file, one object per element, for Blender and other tools.

Writes files `Get3DGeometryOfElements`

[export_obj.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Workflows/export_obj.py)

### What you can do *today.*

Twelve kinds of work offices automate with Tapir, from a palette script to a Grasshopper definition.

#### Property management

Read and update the properties of hundreds of elements in seconds.

#### Geometry generation

Create walls, slabs and beams from Python, with the settings you choose.

#### Quantity take-offs

Material and element quantities for reports, straight from the model.

#### AI assistants (MCP)

Let an AI assistant read and change your model through a Tapir MCP server.

#### BCF issue tracking

Create and track issues and exchange them as BCF files from Python.

#### Classification mapping

Classify elements by naming conventions or by rules on their geometry.

#### Views and layouts

Script views, sections and the Layout Book.

#### Model checking

Find missing values and elements that break the office's standards.

#### Office workflows

Python scripts made for your office's standards, run from the palette.

#### Grasshopper links

Connect Rhino and Grasshopper definitions to native Archicad elements.

#### Element filtering

Select elements by type, layer, classification or nested properties.

#### Bulk renaming

Rename views, layouts and Publisher Sets to match the project's standards.

### One file, *no packages.*

With a project open, Archicad answers JSON commands on `http://127.0.0.1:19723`. Tapir's commands go through Archicad's `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`. Save this as `walls.py` and run it with any Python 3.

With several Archicads open, the next ones answer on 19724, 19725 and so on.

[Your first Python script, step by step →](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python)

walls.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(command, parameters=None):
    body = json.dumps({
        'command': 'API.ExecuteAddOnCommand',
        'parameters': {
            'addOnCommandId': {'commandNamespace': 'TapirCommand', 'commandName': command},
            'addOnCommandParameters': parameters or {}
        }
    }).encode('utf-8')
    request = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:19723', body, {'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        result = json.loads(response.read())
    if not result['succeeded']:
        raise RuntimeError(result['error'])
    return result['result']['addOnCommandResponse']

print(run_tapir_command('GetAddOnVersion'))
walls = run_tapir_command('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
print(len(walls), 'walls')
```

## Get *started.*

From download to your first script in about ten minutes. Steps 1 to 3 need no programming.

 Video Prefer watching? The [Tapir video tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) walk through installing Tapir and using it.

### Install Tapir

With the installer (recommended). It finds every Archicad version on the computer and installs the matching add-on into each, so Archicad loads it on its next start.

[Download WINDOWS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Win.exe) [Download MACOS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Mac.zip)

  - Windows: the installer asks for administrator rights, because it copies the add-on into the Archicad folder under Program Files.
  - macOS: unzip the download and open the app.

Prefer to install by hand? Download the `TapirAddOn_AC<version>_Win.apx` or `TapirAddOn_AC<version>_Mac.zip` file for your Archicad version from the [latest release](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest), then in Archicad: *Options > Add-On Manager > Edit List of Available Add-Ons > Add*, browse to the file and click *OK*.

Tapir keeps itself up to date: it tells you when a new version is out and installs it for you.

### Run your first script

Tapir adds a *Tapir* menu to Archicad. Choose *Tapir Palette* from it, pick a script in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. The built-in scripts are there from the start: try *ProjectHealthCheck*, which lists elements without an ID, zones with the same number, unclassified elements and more. It only reads the model.

Tapir runs the scripts with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which brings the Python and the packages each script needs. If uv is not installed yet, Tapir offers to install it the first time you run a script.

*Manage Shortcuts* on the palette puts up to six scripts in the Tapir menu, as *Run Script Shortcut 1* to *6*.

### Add more scripts

The [Scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/) page collects scripts shared by the community, each one reviewed before it is listed. The Tapir palette is getting a window to find and install them in one click.

 Until then If your palette has no such window yet, add a script by hand, as below.

Download the scripts you want into a folder, then tell Tapir about that folder in its configuration file, `Documents/Tapir/config.json` in your user folder (Tapir writes it the first time it runs). Add the folder to its `localFolders` list, keeping the rest of the file as it is:

Documents/Tapir/config.jsonJSON

```
{
    "repositories": [ ... ],
    "localFolders": [
        {
            "displayName": "My scripts",
            "path": "C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\Tapir scripts"
        }
    ],
    ...
}
```

  - `path` is the folder (on macOS for example `/Users/me/Documents/Tapir scripts`). In JSON, a Windows path's backslashes are doubled.
  - `displayName` is the name the palette shows for the folder's scripts; without it, the folder's name is used.
  - Optionally, `includePattern` and `excludePattern` are regular expressions that choose which files of the folder the palette lists.

The palette lists the folder's scripts next to the built-in ones the next time it loads its scripts.

### Write a script of your own

Archicad answers JSON commands on `http://127.0.0.1:19723` while a project is open (with several Archicads open, the next ones use 19724, 19725 and so on). Tapir's commands are called through Archicad's `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` command, in the `TapirCommand` namespace. Python's standard library is enough; there are no packages to install.

version.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(command, parameters=None):
    request = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:19723')
    request.add_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    body = json.dumps({
        'command': 'API.ExecuteAddOnCommand',
        'parameters': {
            'addOnCommandId': {'commandNamespace': 'TapirCommand', 'commandName': command},
            'addOnCommandParameters': parameters or {}
        }
    }).encode('utf-8')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, body) as response:
        result = json.loads(response.read())
    if not result['succeeded']:
        raise RuntimeError(result['error'])
    return result['result']['addOnCommandResponse']

print(run_tapir_command('GetAddOnVersion'))
## prints the version of the add-on Archicad has loaded, e.g. {'version': '1.8.0'}
```

Graphisoft's [`archicad` package](https://pypi.org/project/archicad/) sends the same commands and finds the port by itself, if you prefer it. Put your script in a [local folder](#marketplace) to run it from the Tapir palette.

[All commands, with schemas and examples →](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/)

### Use it from Grasshopper

In Rhino, open the Package Manager (the `PackageManager` command, or *Tools > Package Manager*), search for tapir, install it and restart Rhino. Its components are on the *Tapir* tab in Grasshopper and work with the Archicad that runs Tapir. The Walls, Doors, Windows and Railings components read and change Archicad elements with the names you know from Archicad's settings dialogs.

[The Grasshopper guide →](https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/)

### How it *works.*

Tapir is an Archicad add-on that turns native API functions into a stateless JSON server on port 19723. Anything that can send an HTTP request can drive Archicad.

GrasshopperThe tapir components

Python scriptsThe palette, or your own

AI and MCPAssistants and MCP servers

Tapir Add-OnA stateless JSON layer: one command per request

ArchicadThe BIM model and its C++ API

### Anatomy of a call

requestPOST 127.0.0.1:19723

```
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {
   "addOnCommandId": {
     "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
     "commandName": "GetElementsByType"},
   "addOnCommandParameters": {
     "elementType": "Wall"}}}
```

response200

```
{"succeeded": true,
 "result": {
   "addOnCommandResponse": {
     "elements": [
       {"elementId": {"guid": "3F2A…"}},
       …
     ]}}}
```

Every Tapir command is sent the same way; only `commandName` and `addOnCommandParameters` change. [Your first Python script →](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python)

## Share a script *from Archicad.*

No GitHub account, no setup. Your name stays on it, and everyone who uses Tapir can install it.

### What happens

1. Send itPost the script in `#share-a-script` on Discord, with a few words on what it does. The Tapir palette is getting a Share button that does the same: you see the whole file before anything is sent. It arrives as a GitHub issue labelled `script-share`.
2. Adapted for any officeTapir's bot, an AI, opens a pull request: hard-coded layers, properties and paths become settings, risky code is removed, and it works in every Archicad language, in metric and imperial.
3. You confirm, it's listedTry the adapted version and say it still does what you meant. Once the pull request is reviewed and merged, it appears on the [Scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/) page with your name.

### Three ways to send it

Coming to the palette

#### From the Tapir palette

Right-click your script and choose Share: add a few words about it and send. Until your palette has it, use Discord.

Easiest today

#### On Discord

Post the script in the `#share-a-script` channel, with a few words on what it does and which Archicad version you use.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

If you use GitHub

#### As a pull request

Add a folder `marketplace/<name>/` with the script, a `listing.json` and a README, as the marketplace README describes.

[The marketplace folder](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/marketplace)

What is sent

#### Only the script

The file, your one-line description, the name to credit, and your Archicad and Tapir versions. Nothing from the open project.

Licence

#### Free for everyone

Every shared script is free and open source. Unless you choose another open-source licence, yours is published under the [MIT licence](https://opensource.org/license/mit): anyone may use, change and share it, as long as they keep your name and the licence with it. It comes without warranty. You stay its author, and its page credits you.

Only share a script you wrote, or one whose author agreed to share it.

### What the AI *changes.*

It keeps what your script does. It changes how, so the script is safe and works in other offices, and lists every change in plain words in the pull request.

Made safe

#### Removed, or flagged for a maintainer

- connections to anything other than Archicad on your own computer;
- running other programs or code built from text (`subprocess`, `os.system`, `eval`, `exec`);
- installing packages while it runs (`pip install`);
- deleting or overwriting files, and writing anywhere but the project's folder and `Documents/Tapir`;
- passwords, tokens and keys;
- user names, `C:\Users\…` paths, and project, client and office names, in the code and its comments.

Made to fit other offices

#### Settings instead of your names

- Property names, layers, stories, paths and classification codes you typed in become settings at the top of the script, or fields of its window.
- Built-in properties are found by their ID, so the script works in every language of Archicad.
- Lengths and areas work in metric and imperial units; paths work on Windows and macOS.

Made safe to run

#### No surprises

- It says what it is about to change, and does nothing, saying so, when nothing fits.
- It makes its changes in one Undo step where it can.
- When a property or element type it needs is missing, it shows a clear message instead of crashing.

Described

#### A README in plain words

- What it does, how to use it, its settings, what it changes, its limits, and *Original by* you.
- Its category, the Archicad and Tapir versions it works with, and whether it changes the model, writes files or only reads.

Before it is merged

#### What the review checks

Every pull request is reviewed before it is merged, like any other code in Tapir. The review checks that:

- nothing on the *Made safe* list is left in, unless a maintainer agreed to it;
- the script still does what you wrote it for, and you confirmed that;
- the folder has the files and fields the [marketplace format](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/marketplace/README.md) asks for;
- the README is accurate, and the screenshots show no client, project or people.

Next step

#### Post your script

Share it in `#share-a-script` on Discord, and we take it from there.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY) [Browse scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/)

Source: https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Docs](https://archicad-api.com/docs/) / Grasshopper

## Grasshopper, *visually.*

The Tapir plugin connects Grasshopper to a running Archicad: read elements and their settings, change them, and create new ones from Rhino geometry, without writing code.

### What the components *do.*

Each component sends a Tapir command to Archicad and gives you the answer as Grasshopper data. You find them on the Tapir tab, grouped as in Archicad.

READElements and their dataElements by type, story or selection; their properties, classifications, settings and geometry.

CHANGEWhat you pass inProperty values, classifications, layers, IDs and tool settings of the elements you pass in.

CREATEFrom Rhino geometryWalls, doors, windows, railings, level dimensions and more, from points and curves.

PROJECTThe rest of the fileStories, attributes, navigator views, layouts, issues, favorites and libraries.

Which Tapir commands have a component, and which settings each covers, is on the [Grasshopper coverage](https://archicad-api.com/gh-coverage/) page.

### One per Archicad *tool.*

A tool component works like the Archicad tool of the same name. One JSON input and one JSON output per panel of its settings dialog, keyed by the labels you see there, such as `Wall Height`.

Design Tools

#### Walls

Placed by `StartPoint` and `EndPoint`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Doors

Placed in an `OwnerWall` at a `CenterOffset`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Windows

Placed in an `OwnerWall` at a `CenterOffset`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Railings

Placed along a `ReferenceLine`.

Refresh Create

Document Tools

#### LevelDimensions

Placed at a `Position`, optionally on a parent element.

Refresh Create

REFRESHReadsReads the elements in `ElementGuid` and fills every output.

EXECUTEWritesWrites the given settings to those elements. Only the keys you give are written.

CREATEMakes new elementsFrom the geometry inputs, starting from the tool's defaults or from a `FavoriteName`.

Nothing is written to Archicad until you press Execute or Create. A JSON output read by Refresh can be fed straight back into the same input. Archicad has no command to change railings or level dimensions after they are placed, so for those Execute only writes the ID, layer and draw order.

 Note Walls remembers the walls its Create made, in the `.gh` file. The next Create updates them instead of making new ones. Turn this off, or forget them, in the component's menu.

### Install

#### Install the Tapir Add-On in Archicad

The components talk to Archicad through the Add-On. [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows how.

#### Install the tapir package in Rhino

In Rhino 7 or 8, open *Tools > Package Manager* (or type `PackageManager`), search for tapir and click Install. Restart Rhino.

#### Open Archicad, then Grasshopper

With a project open in Archicad, start Grasshopper. The Tapir tab appears in its toolbar. With more than one Archicad open, give the port of the one you want to the ConnectArchicad component (*Tapir > General*); the first Archicad uses 19723.

### One *wall.*

Build this in an empty Grasshopper canvas, with a project open in Archicad:

1. Place two Point parameters and set them to 0,0,0 and 5,0,0. Archicad reads the numbers as metres.
2. Place the Walls component from *Tapir > Design Tools*. Connect the points to `StartPoint` and `EndPoint`.
3. Place a Panel with the text on the right and connect it to `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON`.
4. Press Create. A 5 m wall appears in Archicad, 3 m high and 30 cm thick.
5. Move a point and press Create again: the same wall moves. Change the panel and press Create: the same wall changes.

Press Refresh to see every setting of the wall in the JSON outputs. Copy a key from there to set it the next time.

Panel → GeometryAndPositioning_JSONJSON

```
{"Wall Height": 3.0, "Wall Thickness": 0.3}
```

## Tapir and *AI.*

An AI assistant can read your Archicad project and change it through Tapir. You ask in plain words; it sends the commands to the Archicad running on your computer.

### Two ways to *connect.*

Both talk to the same Tapir commands on port 19723, on your own computer.

While you chat

#### An MCP server

The AI tool calls Tapir's commands itself, while you chat. Works with tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), such as Claude Desktop.

[Tapir MCP servers](#mcp-servers)

Any AI tool

#### A script the AI writes

Any AI tool can write a short Python script that sends Tapir commands. You read it, then run it from the Tapir palette or a terminal.

[How it works](#scripts)

### Tapir MCP *servers.*

These are community projects, not part of Tapir. Each has its own install steps in its README. Which one Tapir recommends is still being decided in [issue #2070](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/2070), so they are listed here without a recommendation.

By SzamosiMate

#### tapir-archicad-MCP

The MCP server for Tapir that the others started from. It is also published on PyPI as the tapir-archicad-mcp package.

[Its repository](https://github.com/SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP) [The package on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tapir-archicad-mcp/)

By the community

#### Its forks

Versions of it that others changed and published. Check when each was last updated.

[See the forks](https://github.com/SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP/forks)

 Careful An MCP server can change your model. Try it on a copy of your project first, and read what the AI is about to do before you allow it.

### Start by *reading.*

Open a project in Archicad, with the Tapir Add-On loaded, and give your AI tool this prompt. It only reads, so it is safe to try on any project.

When the answer looks right, ask for a change in the same plain words, and say exactly which elements it may change: "Set the property X to Y on the selected walls only."

promptread only

```
Use Tapir to look at the Archicad project I have open.
Do not change anything; only read.
1. List the stories with their names and levels.
2. Count the walls, slabs, columns, doors and windows on each story.
3. Show the result as one table, one row per story.
Tell me which Tapir commands you used.
```

### Describe it, *run it.*

Without an MCP server, describe the task, give the AI the command list, and run the script it writes.

01Describe what you wantFor example: "Extract all composite exterior walls on level 2 and calculate their net volume."

02Share the command listGive the AI the [command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/) and the working example below. Ask for Python's standard library only, on port 19723.

03Read it, then run itRead the script before you run it, from the Tapir palette or a terminal. Try one that changes the model on a copy of your project first.

promptfor Claude or any AI tool

```
Write a Python script that uses only the standard
library and sends Tapir commands to Archicad on
http://127.0.0.1:19723, like the example I attach.
Use the Tapir command reference I attach.

Extract all composite exterior walls on level 2
and calculate their net volume.

Only read the model; change nothing.
```

tapir_example.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(name, parameters=None, port=19723):
    request = {
        "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
        "parameters": {
            "addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": name},
            "addOnCommandParameters": parameters or {},
        },
    }
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", json.dumps(request).encode("utf-8")) as response:
        answer = json.loads(response.read())
    if not answer.get("succeeded"):
        raise RuntimeError(answer.get("error"))
    return answer["result"]["addOnCommandResponse"]

print(run_tapir_command("GetAddOnVersion"))
```

## Ask. Report. *Test.*

Architects, developers and the maintainers in one place. Bugs and ideas become fixes that someone with your Archicad version tests before they ship.

### Where to find us

Discord

#### Ask anything

Architects, developers and the maintainers, in one server. Show what you made and talk with the people who build Tapir.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

YouTube

#### Learn the API

A video series from the first command to full workflows.

[Watch the tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/)

AI assistants

#### Talk to your model

MCP servers let Claude and other assistants read and change a project through Tapir.

[Tapir and AI](https://archicad-api.com/ai/)

### How the bots *work.*

Most fixes are written by bots and checked by people. The maintainers set the rules and can stop any change; you decide whether a fix works in your Archicad.

01Post itDescribe the bug or idea on Discord or GitHub. A GitHub account is not needed on Discord.

02An issueEvery half hour, Discord posts that read like a bug report or a feature request become GitHub issues, and the bot replies with the link.

03A draft fixThe issue bot answers, asks for what it is missing, or writes the fix and opens a pull request. It is built for every Archicad version and reviewed.

04You testA comment on the pull request links the built add-on and asks the person who reported it to try it.

05ReleasedGreen and reviewed, it is merged three days later unless a maintainer stops it, and ships in Monday's [release](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases).

Report

#### How to report a bug

Post it on Discord or open an issue on GitHub; both reach the same place. A report that can be fixed in one go says:

- your Archicad version and build, and its language (for example 29.0.0 (3100) INT);
- your Tapir version (the *About Tapir* dialog shows it);
- what you did: the script or Grasshopper definition, or the command and the JSON you sent;
- what you expected and what happened instead, with the error message;
- whether the project is a Teamwork project, and which libraries are loaded, when it matters.

 Public Issues and Discord channels are public. Leave out client names, project names and file paths you don't want to share.

[Open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/new) [Post on Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

Test

#### How to test a fix

A fix is only known to work once someone has run it in Archicad. The bots can build Tapir but cannot run Archicad, so your test is what matters most.

1. Open the pull request linked from your issue. A comment on it lists the downloads, one per Archicad version and platform. Downloading needs a GitHub login.
2. Unzip the download for your Archicad version. On macOS it holds another zip with the `.bundle`.
3. In Archicad, open *Options > Add-On Manager > Edit List of Available Add-Ons*, remove or disable the installed Tapir, then *Add* the `.apx` (Windows) or `.bundle` (macOS) and click OK.
4. Do what went wrong before, in a copy of your project.
5. Say on the pull request whether it works and fixes your case. Afterwards, put your installed Tapir back the same way.

Testing often? The [community test runner](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/tools/community-test-runner/GUIDE.md) tests open pull requests on your own Archicad while it is closed, leaves your Tapir in place and posts the result. It runs on Windows and needs Python and a GitHub account.

## What's *next.*

Tapir grows from requests. Most new commands, components and fixes start as a message from someone who needed them in their own work.

### How to ask for a *feature.*

Four steps from "I need this" to a Monday release.

#### Say what you want to do

Post it on Discord or open an issue on GitHub. Describe the task in Archicad, not only the command: "number the doors along a line", "read the area of every zone". A Discord message that reads like a feature request becomes a GitHub issue by itself, labelled `enhancement`.

#### Asking for a part of the Archicad API?

The [API coverage](https://archicad-api.com/api-coverage/) page lists every function of the Archicad API and whether Tapir has a command for it. Use the *Archicad API request* issue form to ask for one that is missing.

#### The issue bot picks it up

A clear, wanted request is built like a fix: the bot writes it and opens a pull request, and you are asked to try it. A large one is split into parts. When the design is open, the bot describes the choices and a maintainer decides.

#### It ships on a Monday

Merged changes are released every Monday. The release notes list them, and the add-on offers to update itself.

### What is being asked for now

[ Requests

#### Open feature requests

Every open issue labelled `enhancement`. Add a comment or a reaction to one you need too.

See the requests → ](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aenhancement) [ Plan

#### Project board

The maintainers' board of planned and ongoing work.

Open the board → ](https://github.com/orgs/ENZYME-APD/projects/4/views/1) [ In progress

#### Open pull requests

Changes being built, reviewed and tested right now.

See the pull requests → ](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/pulls) [ Shipped

#### Releases

Every release, with its notes and downloads. The command reference shows the version each command came in.

See the releases → ](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases)

### Already *here.*

Asked for on the old site's "What's cooking" list, and now part of Tapir.

#### Stairs, roofs and curtain walls

Read and change them: [`ModifyStairs`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyStairs), [`ModifyRoofs`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyRoofs) and [`ModifyCurtainWalls`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWalls).

#### Building materials and composites

Create them from a script: [`CreateBuildingMaterials`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateBuildingMaterials) and [`CreateComposites`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateComposites).

#### Dialogs from Python

A script shows its own window in Archicad: [`ShowScriptUI`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ShowScriptUI) and [`GetScriptUIResult`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetScriptUIResult).

#### 2D detailing

Lines, fills and text: [`CreateLineElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLineElements), [`CreateHatches`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHatches) and [`CreateTexts`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateTexts).

#### Your own properties

Add property definitions from a script: [`CreatePropertyDefinitions`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePropertyDefinitions).

#### Built-in scripts

Ready to run from the palette, from numbering to a project health check. [See them on GitHub](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/builtin-scripts).

## About *Tapir.*

An open-source project that makes Archicad scriptable for architects, not only for programmers. Started in 2022, released every week since.

### Why it *exists.*

Archicad's own JSON API covers only part of what its add-on API can do. Tapir adds the missing commands as an add-on, then puts them within reach of people who don't code: a palette of ready scripts, Grasshopper components, and AI assistants.

### The people *behind it.*

ENZYME-APD runs the project and publishes Tapir under the MIT licence. Everyone below has written code for it, or tested it and given the feedback it is built on, in alphabetical order.

### Principles

FREENo price, everMIT licence for the add-on, the plugin and every shared script.

OPENBuilt in publicEvery issue, pull request and review is on GitHub.

SIGNEDSafe to installThe Windows installer is signed through SignPath; the macOS installer and add-ons are signed and notarized.

WEEKLYSmall, steady releasesA release every Monday when something changed.

### Support *Tapir.*

Tapir is free and open source. This is how it stays up to date with every Archicad version and keeps growing.

Everyone

#### Community crowdfunding

Small contributions from many users make a big difference: regular small pledges can fund maintainers who update Tapir for each new Archicad version.

Practices and firms

#### Corporate sponsoring

Offices and engineering firms that use Tapir in their own R&D sponsor the commands their projects need, and those commands then serve everyone.

Your office

#### Training and services

Training sessions, implementation workshops and custom development for offices moving to computational BIM workflows with Tapir.

Talk to us: contact@enzyme-apd.com

Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation. Archicad is a trademark of Graphisoft SE; Tapir is not made by Graphisoft.

## Scripts in the Tapir palette

- **Automatic Numbering Based on Polyline**: Select one polyline and the elements to number. The elements get their Element ID in the order they follow along the polyline, from its first point to its last one. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline.py))
- **Batch Publisher**: Publishes the chosen Publisher Sets in one go, now or on a schedule (every N minutes or hours, or daily at a given time on the chosen weekdays). Before publishing it can receive the Teamwork changes and update the drawings on the layouts. The schedule runs while this window is open. The settings are saved per project, the runs are logged in the window and in a CSV file next to the settings (Documents/Tapir). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BatchPublisher.py))
- **Building Material Property Audit**: Lists the value of a custom property for every Building Material of the project, so the materials with an empty value stand out. Export the list to Excel or CSV, or give the chosen materials a value: the script shows which materials it will change and asks before changing them, then reports the materials it could not change. Based on the audit_building_material_properties.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BuildingMaterialPropertyAudit.py))
- **Bulk View Renamer**: Lists the views of the View Map, or of one of its folders, and renames them in one go: find and replace (optionally a regular expression), a prefix and a suffix, or a pattern with a counter. A table shows the old and the new name of every view with name clashes marked, and nothing is renamed until you confirm. The views are renamed one by one with RenameNavigatorItem, and every view that could not be renamed is reported. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BulkViewRenamer.py))
- **Classification Overview**: Shows how many elements are classified with each item of a classification system, as a tree that follows the system's hierarchy, plus the elements that have no classification in it. Select items to highlight their elements, double-click one to select its elements in Archicad, and export the counts to Excel or CSV. Based on the get_elements_by_classification.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ClassificationOverview.py))
- **Complex Element Finder**: Finds the elements that make the project heavy: polylines, fills, slabs and other polygonal elements with too many points in their outline, and elements whose 3D model has too many polygons (imported objects, morphs, detailed library parts). Lists them, highlights them in red and selects them in Archicad on request. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ComplexElementFinder.py))
- **Distribution Board Schedule**: Lists the circuits of every distribution board with their loads, totals each board and its phases, flags the circuits over a load limit and the boards whose phases are out of balance, and saves the schedule as CSV or Excel. It only reads the project. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DistributionBoardSchedule.py))
- **Door and Window Numbering by Zone**: Gives every door and window an Element ID built from the zone it opens into, such as 1.04-D1 or 1.04-W2, numbered within each zone. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DoorWindowNumberingByZone.py))
- **Drawing Status Report**: Lists every Drawing placed on the layouts of the Layout Book with the columns of Archicad's Drawing Manager: status, update type, stored in project, source and path. Export the list to Excel or CSV, or update the drawings whose source has changed: the script shows which drawings it will update and asks before updating them, then reports the drawings it could not update. Reading opens each layout in turn (Archicad gives a drawing's data only from its own layout) and then goes back to the window that was active. Based on the get_drawing_manager_data.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DrawingStatusReport.py))
- **Electrical and Plumbing Check**: Before drawings are issued, lists the electrical and plumbing symbols that miss data: GDL symbols whose circuit, board or number parameter (chosen by the user) is empty or names a board that does not exist, Archicad 30 electrical devices that are not connected to a circuit, Archicad 30 circuits without devices, and sanitary objects that are outside every zone. Each group can be highlighted and selected in Archicad. The script only reads the model; it changes nothing but the highlight and the selection. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ElectricalPlumbingCheck.py))
- **Material Take-Off**: Totals the volume (m³) and the projected area (m²) of every building material used by the walls, columns, beams, slabs, roofs and shells, per story and optionally per element type, from the quantities Archicad calculates for each skin. The table can be copied to the clipboard or saved as Excel or CSV for a bill of quantities. It only reads the project. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/MaterialTakeOff.py))
- **Missing Library Parts**: Lists the library parts the placed Objects, Lamps, Windows and Doors use but the loaded libraries do not have (the elements Archicad shows as dots, e.g. after migrating a project), with the elements that use each one, per story. The elements can be selected in Archicad, or switched to a loaded library part with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Nothing is changed before the list of elements to change is confirmed; a report then shows the result of each one. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/MissingLibraryParts.py))
- **Object Counter**: Counts the placed objects, lamps, doors, windows and (from Archicad 30) electrical devices by library part, grouped by story and by the zone they stand in. The zone is found from the element's position and the zone polygons of its story. Optionally it also sums one numeric GDL parameter, for example a fixture's load or its drainage fixture units. The table can be saved as CSV or Excel. The script only reads the model; it changes nothing in it (it can select the counted elements). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ObjectCounter.py))
- **Non-orthogonal Wall Finder**: Lists the walls that are not aligned to the allowed angle grid (every 90° or every 45°), highlights them in red and selects them in Archicad on request. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/OrthoWallFinder.py))
- **Place Symbols in Rooms**: Places a library part in the chosen zones by a rule: - along the zone's boundary at a spacing and a mounting height, keeping a distance from the corners and the doors (for example sockets), or - in a grid with a maximum spacing and a margin from the walls (for example lights). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PlaceSymbolsInRooms.py))
- **Project Health Check**: Runs quality checks on the model and lists what it finds: elements without an Element ID, zones with the same number, unclassified elements, duplicate elements in the same place, very small elements, elements far from the project origin, elements on hidden layers, stories without elements and layers that no floor plan element uses. The findings can be highlighted and selected in Archicad, exported to Excel or CSV, and turned into Issues. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ProjectHealthCheck.py))
- **Property Highlighter**: Colors the elements in the model by the value of a chosen property, with a legend of the values and their element counts. Text values get one color each; number values can also be grouped into ranges with a color gradient. Select values in the legend to highlight only those, double-click one to select its elements in Archicad. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyHighlighter.py))
- **Property Value Exporter**: Writes the values of the chosen properties of the chosen element types into an Excel workbook or a CSV file, one row per element, without changing anything in the project. It replaces building an interactive schedule only to copy its values into Excel. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py))
- **Room Finishes Schedule**: Lists the floor, wall and ceiling finish areas of every zone (or of the selected zones), one row per zone and finish, and saves the table as CSV or Excel. It reads only; nothing in the project is changed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/RoomFinishesSchedule.py))
- **Run Lengths**: Totals the lengths of pipe, duct and wiring runs in two ways, side by side: the MEP Modeler routes and flexible segments per domain, MEP system and size, and the 2D lines, polylines and arcs drawn for them, per layer, pen or line type. In Archicad 30 each electrical circuit's estimated cable length is listed as well. The table can be copied or saved as CSV or Excel. It reads only; nothing in the project is changed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/RunLengths.py))
- **Solid Operation Explorer**: Lists the solid element operation links (target, operation, operator) of the elements, highlights the targets and operators, and finds the links that have no effect any more because the two elements do not touch. The chosen links can be removed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/SolidOperationExplorer.py))
- **Story Setup**: Sets up the stories of the project from a table: paste it (name and level or height per row, from Excel or any text) or load a CSV file. The current stories are shown next to the new ones with what would be added, renamed, moved and deleted, and nothing changes until you press Apply. A table that would delete a story with elements on it is refused. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/StorySetup.py))
- **Find and Replace in Texts**: Searches the content of every Text and text Label (the selection, the current story or the whole project), with match case and whole word options. Every match is listed with its story and a preview of the changed line, with a checkbox per match; only the checked matches are replaced. The replacement is written with ChangeTextContent, so the styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it stay as they are. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/TextFindReplace.py))
- **Unused View Cleaner**: Finds the views of the View Map that are neither placed on a layout nor published by a Publisher Set, and moves the chosen ones into a separate folder that repeats their original folder structure. A clone folder is only moved as a whole, when none of its views is used. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/UnusedViewCleaner.py))
- **Zone Area Check**: Compares the measured area of every zone with a target area read from a property you choose, within a tolerance in percent. Lists the zones that are over, under and on target, and highlights them in three colors. It changes nothing in the project apart from the highlight. Select rows to highlight only those zones, double-click one to select it in Archicad, and export the list to Excel or CSV. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ZoneAreaCheck.py))


---

# Command reference (one line each)

Parameters and results of each: https://archicad-api.com/commands.md. ## Application Commands

- **GetAddOnVersion** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.
- **GetArchicadLocation** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.
- **GetArchicadReleaseInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the main version, release version and build number of the running Archicad, with the caption of its window.
- **GetPrinterInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves Archicad's current print settings: the print area, grid, fixed text size and scale (the settings PrintView takes).
- **GetPrinterAndPlotterInfo** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the printer selected in Archicad, with its name and orientation, and the selected plotter, with its name and model.
- **QuitArchicad** (since 0.1.0): Performs a quit operation on the currently running Archicad instance.
- **GetPointFromUser** (since 1.5.9): Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled. Parameters: prompt.
- **ModelToScreen** (since 1.8.0): Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: coordinates.
- **ScreenToModel** (since 1.8.0): Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel. Parameters: screenPoints.
- **GetElementFromUser** (since 1.7.3): Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled. Parameters: prompt, elementTypes.
- **GetLineFromUser** (since 1.8.0): Waits for the user to input a line in the active Archicad window and returns start and end coordinates. Parameters: startPrompt, endPrompt, showRubberLineFeedback.
- **GetPolygonFromUser** (since 1.8.0): Waits for the user to input a polygon in the active Archicad window and returns its points and arcs. Parameters: startPrompt, prompt, method.
- **GetCurrentWindowType** (since 1.0.7): Returns the type of the current (active) window and, when it has one, the databaseId of the database it shows, which ChangeWindow takes to bring the window back after a script switched to another one. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned, as Archicad does not tell which one it was.
- **GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale** (since 1.7.3): Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.
- **SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale** (since 1.7.3): Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable. Parameters: scale, rebuild.
- **ChangeWindow** (since 1.3.1): Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. The databaseId of a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened opens its Project Map item instead (from Archicad 27). With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan. windowType 'Report' on its own opens the Session Report window (from Archicad 26); its text cannot be read through the Archicad API.
- **GetContainingDatabases** (since 1.7.3): Returns the database (window type, database id and name) that contains each of the given elements, from any database, not only the current one. Pass the windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it, for example to find an element placed on a layout. Parameters: elements.
- **CloseWindows** (since 1.8.0): Closes the windows of the given databases (for example layouts, sections or details opened earlier with ChangeWindow), with one execution result per window; a window Archicad cannot close gets a failed result. Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: windows.
- **RebuildCurrentDatabase** (since 1.8.0): Rebuilds the current database, the one the API works on (see ChangeWindow). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **DeleteGhostRecords** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the trace (ghost) record of each given parent database, which removes the trace reference shown in that database's window. A database without a trace reference gets a failed execution result. Not undoable. Parameters: databases.
- **GetUserGSID** (since 1.5.6): Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **ShowAlert** (since 1.5.6): Display a dialog with up to three buttons. Parameters: alertType, title, message, subMessage, button1, button2, button3.
- **GetSpecialFolders** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.). Parameters: folderTypes.
- **GetEditModeState** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether Archicad is in a hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing), and which element is being edited. Read only: it never enters, leaves or cancels an editing mode. Commands that modify the project can fail while such a mode is active. The overall inEditMode flag requires Archicad 29 or later; the command requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **GetArchicadVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Returns whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden. Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
- **SetArchicadVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Hides or shows the Archicad application, e.g. to keep it out of the way while a batch runs. A script that hides Archicad must show it again, also when the script fails (e.g. in a finally block). Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error. Parameters: isVisible.
- **RunActionCenterChecks** (since 1.8.0): Runs the given checks of the Action Center (by default the hotlink check). A successful result means the check ran, not that nothing was found: Archicad does not report the outcome to the caller, it shows the Action Center tab when the check found an issue. Parameters: checks.
- **RedrawCurrentDatabase** (since 1.8.0): Redraws the current database, even when its window is in the background. Only the visible region of its window is updated.
- **GetProductVersionInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the version information of the running Archicad: build number, language code, product family and version text, plus the product name, product type, main/update/hotfix versions, the available domains (Architecture, MEP) and the CEIP project identifier of the open project from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
- **Get3DCutawayStatus** (since 1.7.3): Returns whether 3D Cutaway is on and whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
- **Set3DCutawayStatus** (since 1.7.3): Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open. Parameters: cutawayEnabled, cuttingPlanesVisible.
- **SetDialogAutoClose** (since 1.7.3): Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it. Parameters: enabled.
- **GetDialogAutoClose** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the dialog auto close is on, the same state SetDialogAutoClose writes, so a script can restore it afterwards. The state belongs to the running Archicad process: it is off when Archicad starts (unless the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable is true), it stays as last set until Archicad quits, and it is shared by every add-on and script in that Archicad.

## Project Commands

- **GetProjectInfo** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.
- **GetProjectInfoFields** (since 0.1.2): Retrieves the names and values of all project info fields.
- **SetProjectInfoField** (since 0.1.2): Sets the value of a project info field. Parameters: projectInfoId, projectInfoValue.
- **CreateProjectInfoFields** (since 1.5.2): Creates one or more custom project info fields. Parameters: projectInfoFields.
- **DeleteProjectInfoFields** (since 1.5.4): Deletes one or more custom project info fields. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted. Parameters: projectInfoIds.
- **GetProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the Project Info groups in their order, each with its fields: id, name, value and, when exactly one project info autotext has the name of the field, the autotext key that SetProjectInfoField takes. Available from Archicad 30.
- **CreateProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Creates Project Info groups with the given names, at the end of the group list. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **RenameProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Renames Project Info groups. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **DeleteProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Deletes Project Info groups. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **MoveProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Moves Project Info groups before another group, or to the end of the group list when no other group is given. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **GetStories** (since 1.1.5): Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.
- **SetStories** (since 1.1.5): Sets the story sructure of the currently loaded project. Parameters: stories.
- **GetAutoTextKeys** (since 1.5.9): Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'. Parameters: elementId.
- **GetAutoTextName** (since 1.5.9): Retrieves the display names of one or more autotext keys (as returned inside a '<...>' embedded key), with a direct guid lookup for property-based keys instead of enumerating every property definition. Parameters: keys.
- **GetNoteAutotexts** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the autotexts available in the notes of an element type (e.g. a Dimension), each with the element types it is available for. The autotexts are identified by the numeric value of their API_NoteAutotextID. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: noteOwnerType.
- **GetNoteAutoTextKeywords** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the keywords of note autotexts (the autotexts of dimension, label and other element notes) by their numeric API_NoteAutotextID values. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: autoTextIds.
- **GetHotlinks** (since 0.1.0): Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.
- **CreateHotlinkNodes** (since 1.5.9): Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node). Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **CreateHotlinkInstances** (since 1.5.9): Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **ChangeHotlinkInstances** (since 1.5.9): Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **UpdateHotlinks** (since 1.7.1): Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **ChangeHotlinkNodes** (since 1.7.1): Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **BreakHotlinkNodes** (since 1.8.0): Breaks hotlink nodes, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does: the elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **DeleteHotlinkNodes** (since 1.8.0): Deletes hotlink nodes together with their placed instances, as the Hotlink Manager's Delete does. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **GetHotlinkOwnersOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Tells for each element whether it comes from a hotlinked module, and returns the hotlink element that contains it and the hotlink instance it belongs to. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetHotlinkProxyElementTable** (since 1.7.3): Maps the proxy elements of placed hotlink instances to the elements of the source file they were made from, so an element seen in a hotlinked module can be traced back to its source element. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **GetHotlinkSourceStatus** (since 1.8.0): Tells for each hotlink source file whether it is available, missing, not accessible, incompatible or offline. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: hotlinks.
- **OpenProject** (since 1.0.7): Opens the given project. Parameters: projectFilePath.
- **NewProject** (since 1.7.3): Starts a new, untitled project from the template set in Archicad's New Project settings, as File > New does; with newAndReset also the working environment is reset, as New and Reset All does. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded, as with OpenProject. Parameters: newAndReset.
- **CloseProject** (since 1.3.1): Closes the currently opened project.
- **SaveProject** (since 1.3.1): Saves the currently opened project. Parameters: projectPath.
- **SaveAsModuleFile** (since 1.5.9): Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file. Parameters: moduleFilePath, elements.
- **SaveProjectAsArchive** (since 1.6.0): Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside. Parameters: archiveFilePath, includeLibraryParts, includeProperties, includeTextures, includeBackgroundPicture.
- **SaveCurrentWindowAsImage** (since 1.7.2): Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format. Master layout windows are not supported: save a layout that uses the master layout instead. Parameters: imageFilePath, format, colorDepth, dithered, entireDrawing.
- **GetCurrentViewImage** (since 1.7.3): Returns what the 3D window, or the PhotoRendering window, shows as a base64 encoded png or jpg image with its size in pixels, without writing a file. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: source, format.
- **GetRenderingScenes** (since 1.8.0): Gets the names of the rendering scenes of the project, as the Scene list of the PhotoRendering Settings palette shows them.
- **SetCurrentRenderingScene** (since 1.8.0): Makes the given rendering scene the current one, as selecting it in the PhotoRendering Settings palette does. Parameters: sceneName.
- **PhotoRender** (since 1.8.0): Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). The image size and quality come from the scene. Parameters: imageFilePath, format, sceneName.
- **GetCalculationUnits** (since 1.4.0): Gets the project calculation units.
- **GetDimensionStandards** (since 1.8.0): Gets the dimension standards of the project (Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions) with their name and the unit, decimals and rounding of each dimension type, optionally only the one with the given name. Read-only. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.
- **GetExportTolerance** (since 1.8.0): Gets the export tolerance: the largest distance allowed between an arc and the straight segments that replace it when curves are segmented for export.
- **GetLast3DDefaultLevels** (since 1.8.0): Gets the last 3D default levels of the given element types' defaults. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **SetLast3DDefaultLevels** (since 1.8.0): Sets the last 3D default levels of the given element types' defaults. Parameters: elementTypes, levels.
- **GetProjectPreferences** (since 1.7.3): Gets pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units and the zones. Further pages may follow. Parameters: preferenceTypes.
- **SetProjectPreferences** (since 1.7.3): Changes pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units and the zones. Only the given fields change, the rest of each page keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: workingUnits, dimensions, calculationUnits, zones.
- **ConvertUnitValues** (since 1.8.0): Formats lengths, areas, volumes and angles (given in meters, square meters, cubic meters and radians) as Archicad shows them with the unit and rounding of the given Project Preference, returning the text, its extra accuracy decimals and the unit. The output is aligned with the input array of values. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: values.
- **GetRenovationStatusNames** (since 1.8.0): Gets the names the running Archicad shows for the renovation statuses Existing, New and Demolished (localized). Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetGeoLocation** (since 1.1.6): Gets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26).
- **GetSurveyPointTransformation** (since 1.7.3): Gets the 3x4 matrix that transforms points from the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row, and its inverse when it is invertible. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGeoLocation** (since 1.2.9): Sets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26). Omitted fields stay unchanged. Parameters: projectLocation, surveyPoint.
- **SetPlaceSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the place settings of the project: location (longitude, latitude, altitude, north), date, time, summer time and time zone. Only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back, with the sun position Archicad calculated for them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: placeInfo.
- **FindDimensionStandard** (since 1.8.0): Finds a dimension standard (Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions) by its name and returns its index, name and guid. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.
- **GetProjectNotes** (since 1.7.3): Gets the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes): client, project name, company, address, architect, draftsmen, project status, date of issue, keywords and notes.
- **SetProjectNotes** (since 1.7.3): Changes the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes). Only the given fields are changed; texts longer than the field Archicad stores are truncated. Parameters: client, projectName, company, street, city, country, postalCode, architect, draftsmen, projectStatus, dateOfIssue, keywords, notes.
- **GetSunSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the project's date and time (Options > Project Preferences > Location Settings), the sun position Archicad calculates for them at the project location, and the sun and ambient light settings.
- **CalculateSunPosition** (since 1.8.0): Calculates the sun position (azimuth and altitude in degrees) for a date and time, at the project location unless another one is given, without changing the project. Parameters: dateTime, location.
- **PrintView** (since 1.3.1): Prints from the current view. Parameters: grid, fixText, scale, printArea.
- **RebuildView** (since 1.5.0): Rebuilds the current view. Parameters: regenerate.
- **GetAutoIntersect** (since 1.8.0): Gets whether Auto-Intersection (Options > Auto-Intersection) is on. It changes what the wall and beam creation commands produce: with it on, the new elements are joined at their intersections.
- **SetAutoIntersect** (since 1.8.0): Turns Auto-Intersection on or off. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project; remember to restore the previous state afterwards. Parameters: isOn.

## Custom Data Commands

- **SetElementUserData** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved. Parameters: elementUserData.
- **GetElementUserData** (since 1.8.0): Reads the values stored on elements by SetElementUserData: every key of each element, or only the given keys. Parameters: elements, keys.

## Element Commands

- **GetSelectedElements** (since 0.1.0): Gets the list of the currently selected elements.
- **GetElementsByType** (since 1.0.7): Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: elementType, filters, databases.
- **GetAllElements** (since 1.0.7): Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: filters, databases.
- **CaptureElementState** (since 1.8.0): Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier. Parameters: type.
- **GetElementChangesSince** (since 1.8.0): Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted. Parameters: stateId, toStateId.
- **ReleaseElementState** (since 1.8.0): Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits. Parameters: stateId.
- **GetElementTypeNames** (since 1.7.3): Gets the localized names of the given element types, as the running Archicad shows them (for example 'Wand' for Wall in German Archicad). The output is aligned with the input array of element types. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **GetElementsInCreationOrder** (since 1.8.0): Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in the order the elements were created. Parameters: databases.
- **ChangeSelectionOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection. Parameters: addElementsToSelection, removeElementsFromSelection.
- **FilterElements** (since 1.0.7): Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices) and element type (elementTypes). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter. Parameters: elements, filters, layerIndices, floorIndices, elementTypes.
- **GetDetailsOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true. Parameters: elements, fields.
- **SetDetailsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Sets the details of the given elements (floor, layer, order, Element ID etc). Parameters: elementsWithDetails.
- **SetElementInfoStrings** (since 1.8.0): Sets the info string of the given elements: the Element ID shown in the Info Box, which GetDetailsOfElements returns as id. Returns one execution result per element. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementCategories** (since 1.7.3): Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.
- **GetCategoryValuesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. Parameters: elements, categories.
- **GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types, the values new elements of the type get, optionally only for the given category types. A category the default has no value in is listed without categoryValueId; an element type without any of the requested categories gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. Parameters: elementTypes, categories.
- **SetCategoryValuesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. Parameters: elementCategoryValues.
- **Get3DBoundingBoxes** (since 1.1.2): Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. An element without 3D geometry of its own gets an error item instead of a bounding box. Parameters: elements.
- **GetLibPartTransformations** (since 1.8.0): Gets the placement transformation of library part instances (Window, Door, Object, Lamp, Zone) as Archicad computes it: the location, the rotation angle and the x/y scaling. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **ConvertRevealOffsets** (since 1.7.3): Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: openings.
- **Get3DGeometryOfElements** (since 1.7.2): Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementConnections** (since 1.8.0): Gets the connections among the given elements: each pair of touching elements once, with the polygons of the surface where they touch, in world coordinates. The 3D model of the elements is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. Also returns, aligned with the input array of elements, whether each element was found. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetBodyMaterialsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the building material of each body of the 3D model of the given elements. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetCutPolygonsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Cuts each body of the 3D model of the given elements with a plane and returns, for each body, its building material, the area of the cut surface and its polygons (outline and holes) in 2D coordinates of the plane. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed.
