The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements, cutPlane.
- **GetElementAtCoordinate** (since 1.7.3): Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser. Parameters: elementType, coordinate, z, filters.
- **GetSkylightHolePolygons** (since 1.8.0): Gets the polygon of the hole each given Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell: the outline and any holes of it as 2D coordinates. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element that is not a Skylight gets an error item. Parameters: elements.
- **GetVisibleSkinStatus** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether elements have a visible skin in a given Partial Structure Display mode (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly), e.g. a finish-only slab has none in CoreOnly. The current window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, structureDisplay.
- **GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms** (since 1.8.0): Gets the absolute bottom level of curtain walls or their subelements (segments, frames, panels, junctions, accessories). The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetQuantitiesOfElements** (since 1.7.2): Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call. Parameters: elements, minOpeningSize, calculateInOneCall.
- **TriangulatePolygonsOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item. Parameters: elements, convex.
- **GetTextureCoordinates** (since 1.8.0): Gets the texture coordinates (u, v) of the faces of the 3D model of the given elements: per solid body, per face, at the first vertex of the face. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetSurfaceTypesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the surface type of every polygon of the 3D model of the given elements, as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it: for each element its polygons with their body index, polygon index, polygon id and the numeric API_SurfaceTypeID value. The model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **Get3DModelCounts** (since 1.8.0): Gets the number of components of each type (bodies, polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices, normal vectors, materials and lights) in the 3D model Archicad currently holds, as ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum counts them. A type that cannot be counted gets an error item. Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, coverElements.
- **GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements** (since 1.0.6): Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetHierarchicalElementOwners** (since 1.7.3): Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element. Parameters: elements, ownerMode.
- **EditHierarchicalElement** (since 1.8.0): Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Leave the mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing. Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elementId.
- **FinishHierarchicalEditing** (since 1.8.0): Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: accept.
- **GetConnectedElements** (since 1.1.4): Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing. Parameters: elements, connectedElementType.
- **GetElementsInDrawOrder** (since 1.7.3): Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: elementType, filters, databases.
- **GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Returns the 2D drawing primitives (points, lines, arcs, texts, polylines, triangles, polygons, pictures) Archicad draws each given floor plan element from, in drawing order, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrimsExt decomposes it on every story and unclipped. Control items (type Ctrl_*) mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts such as hatches and texts. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetStoryControlPrimitives** (since 1.8.0): Returns the 2D drawing primitives of the story levels (story lines and their markers) drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation database, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_DrawStoryControl draws them, in the same format as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements. The databaseId can be obtained with GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId. Parameters: databaseId.
- **GetSectionElements** (since 1.5.8): Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires. Parameters: databases.
- **GetRelationsOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: elements, otherElementType.
- **LinkElements** (since 1.7.3): Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable. Parameters: links.
- **UnlinkElements** (since 1.7.3): Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable. Parameters: links.
- **GetLinksOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the links created by LinkElements that start from the given elements: the linked element and the flags of each link. Links pointing to an element are not returned; query the elements they start from. Returns an error item for an element that does not exist. Parameters: elements.
- **GetZoneBoundaries** (since 1.2.3): Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone. Parameters: zoneElementId, zones.
- **GetZoneReductions** (since 1.7.3): Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the property objects of the given elements: the library parts of the old listing system (used by projects migrated from older Archicad versions) linked to each element by criteria or individually, with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDescriptorsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the descriptors of the given elements: the listing descriptors in the property objects of each element, with the library part that declares them (index, name and guid), their listing database set and index, and their status (Normal, Deleted or Local). The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, which of them match, and which one is assigned individually, each with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, and which one is assigned individually (0 removes the individual assignment). A link that is not given stays unchanged. All changes are made in one undoable step. Parameters: elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.
- **UpdateZones** (since 1.5.4): Updates all Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements). Parameters: keepStampPosition, undoTopTrim, undoBottomTrim.
- **SetZoneLabelingSettings** (since 1.7.3): Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off and selects the Label Favorite it places. Only the given settings are changed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: automaticLabeling, favoriteName.
- **GetZoneLabelingSettings** (since 1.8.0): Returns whether the automatic labeling of Zones is on and the name of the Label Favorite it places. Available from Archicad 28.
- **GetCollisions** (since 1.2.2): Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements. Parameters: elementsGroup1, elementsGroup2, settings.
- **HighlightElements** (since 1.0.3): Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights. On Archicad 25 nonHighlightedColor is ignored. Parameters: elements, highlightedColors, wireframe3D, nonHighlightedColor.
- **MoveElements** (since 1.0.2): Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithMoveVectors.
- **RotateElements** (since 1.5.3): Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithRotations.
- **MirrorElements** (since 1.7.3): Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithMirrorAxes.
- **DeleteElements** (since 1.2.1): Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted. Parameters: elements.
- **DeleteSelectedElements** (since 1.7.3): Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key.
- **LockElements** (since 1.5.2): Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork! Parameters: elements.
- **UnlockElements** (since 1.5.2): Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork! Parameters: elements.
- **RefreshElements** (since 1.8.0): Refreshes (rebuilds) the given elements, for example placed Objects, Windows and Doors that still show the old geometry after their library part's script or embedded file changed. Set force to true to run the parameter script of GDL-based elements too. The elements are looked up in the current database (floor plan, section or detail window). Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone. Parameters: elements, force.
- **GetGDLParametersOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **SetGDLParametersOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it. Parameters: elementsWithGDLParameters.
- **GetMarkerParametersOfElements** (since 1.7.1): Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Parameters: elements.
- **SetMarkerParametersOfElements** (since 1.7.1): Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are. Parameters: elementsWithMarkerParameters.
- **GetURLReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA. Parameters: elements.
- **SetURLReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. Fails with APIERR_MOREUSER for an element that already holds a link. Parameters: elementsWithURLReferences.
- **ChangeLibraryPartOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B). Parameters: elementsWithLibraryPart.
- **GetHotspotsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the 2D hotspots of the given library part instances (Objects, Lamps, Windows, Doors, Skylights, Zones, Curtain Wall parts, etc.), e.g. to dimension to them. Parameters: elements.
- **RunParameterScriptOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateColumns** (since 1.0.3): Creates Column elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: columnsData.
- **CreateWalls** (since 1.4.0): Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: wallsData.
- **CreateBeams** (since 1.4.0): Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: beamsData.
- **CreateStairs** (since 1.5.0): Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters. Parameters: stairsData.
- **SolveStairBaseline** (since 1.7.3): Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: stairsData.
- **CreateSlabs** (since 1.0.3): Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: slabsData.
- **CreateWindows** (since 1.4.0): Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters. Parameters: windowsData.
- **CreateDoors** (since 1.4.0): Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters. Parameters: doorsData.
- **CreateOpenings** (since 1.4.0): Creates Opening elements in the given host elements. Parameters: openingsData.
- **GetOpeningDefault** (since 1.7.3): Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.
- **SetOpeningDefault** (since 1.8.0): Changes the settings of the Opening tool defaults, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. Only the given settings change. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: extrusionParameters, floorPlanParameters.
- **PlaceOpenings** (since 1.8.0): Places openings with the Opening tool settings at points of their parent elements. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface. Each opening can be given its own extrusion and floor plan settings, which change only that opening and not the tool's settings. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsData.
- **GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters** (since 1.7.3): Returns the floor plan parameters of Opening elements: the floor plan display mode, the divided opening mode, the open edge style, the reference axis, the cut surface and outline lines, the cover fills and the cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters** (since 1.7.3): Changes the floor plan parameters of Opening elements returned by GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, and sets or removes their cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsWithFloorPlanParameters.
- **GetOpeningSymbolParameters** (since 1.8.0): Returns the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of GetGDLParametersOfElements. A symbol the opening does not have is left out. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningSymbolParameters** (since 1.8.0): Changes the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **GetOpeningDetails** (since 1.7.3): Returns the details of Opening elements: whether they exist, the parent element, the cut and connected elements, the geometry (anchor point, extrusion direction, axes, polygon) and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides). Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningDetails** (since 1.7.3): Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsWithDetails.
- **CreateMorphs** (since 1.4.0): Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions. Parameters: morphsData.
- **CreateRoofs** (since 1.4.0): Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead. Parameters: roofsData.
- **CreateRailings** (since 1.8.0): Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices. Parameters: railingsData.
- **CreateCurtainWalls** (since 1.7.2): Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid. Parameters: curtainWallsData.
- **CreateAssociativeDimensions** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative linear dimensions from explicit witness point references. A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative linear dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column and opening presets. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **CreateWallThicknessDimensions** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **GetDimensionData** (since 1.5.0): Gets witness point data (coordinates, measured values) from existing dimension chains. Parameters: elements.
- **GetOpeningTransformations** (since 1.7.3): Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateZones** (since 1.1.8): Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: zonesData.
- **CreatePolylines** (since 1.1.5): Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: polylinesData.
- **CreateLineElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates Line elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: linesData.
- **CreateArcs** (since 1.5.6): Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: arcsData.
- **CreateCircles** (since 1.5.6): Creates Circle elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: circlesData.
- **CreateHotspots** (since 1.5.6): Creates Hotspot elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: hotspotsData.
- **CreateHatches** (since 1.5.6): Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches. Parameters: hatchesData.
- **CreateSplines** (since 1.5.6): Creates Spline elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: splinesData.
- **CreateObjects** (since 1.5.7): Creates Object elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: objectsData.
- **CreateLamps** (since 1.5.7): Creates Lamp elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: lampsData.
- **GetGridElementDefaults** (since 1.7.2): Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.
- **GetGridElements** (since 1.7.2): Lists the grid elements (placed with the Grid Tool or created by CreateGridElements) with their position, angle, size, library part and optionally GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: includeParameters.
- **CreateGridElements** (since 1.7.2): Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: gridElements.
- **CreateMeshes** (since 1.1.9): Creates Mesh elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: meshesData.
- **CreateLabels** (since 1.2.5): Creates Label elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: labelsData.
- **CreateTexts** (since 1.5.0): Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: textsData.
- **CreateLevelDimensions** (since 1.7.2): Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes. Parameters: levelDimensionsData.
- **ModifyWalls** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: wallsWithDetails.
- **ModifyBeams** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: beamsWithDetails.
- **ModifySlabs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: slabsWithDetails.
- **ModifyColumns** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: columnsWithDetails.
- **ModifyWindows** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: windowsWithDetails.
- **ModifyDoors** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: doorsWithDetails.
- **ModifyMorphs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: morphsWithDetails.
- **ModifyRoofs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: roofsWithDetails.
- **ModifyShells** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the structure (Basic or Composite, building material or composite) of Shell elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: shellsWithDetails.
- **ModifyMeshes** (since 1.5.4): Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: meshesData.
- **ModifyObjects** (since 1.5.7): Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: objectsWithDetails.
- **ModifyLamps** (since 1.5.7): Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: lampsWithDetails.
- **ModifyTexts** (since 1.5.9): Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: textsWithDetails.
- **ModifyLabels** (since 1.5.9): Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: labelsWithDetails.
- **ModifyCurtainWalls** (since 1.8.0): Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls. Parameters: curtainWallsWithDetails.
- **ChangeTextContent** (since 1.8.0): Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content. Parameters: contentChanges.
- **ModifyZones** (since 1.8.0): Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link and floor thickness. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon is kept. Parameters: zonesWithDetails.
- **MeasureTexts** (since 1.7.3): Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing. Parameters: texts.
- **GetElementPreviewImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the preview image of the given element. Parameters: elementId, imageType, format, width, height.
- **GetRoomImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the room image of the given zone. Parameters: zoneId, format, width, height, offset, scale, backgroundColor.
- **SetElementNotificationClient** (since 1.2.8): Sets up a new notification client to receive element events. Parameters: host, port, notifyOnNewElement, notifyOnModificationOfAnElement, notifyOnReservationChanges.
- **RemoveElementNotificationClient** (since 1.2.8): Removes an element notification client. Parameters: host, port.
- **RegularizePolygons** (since 1.7.3): Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: polygons, withAncestry.
- **RegularizePolylines** (since 1.7.3): Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: polylines, withAncestry.

## Element grouping Commands

- **CreateGroups** (since 1.4.0): Creates groups of the passed elements Parameters: elementGroups.
- **UngroupElements** (since 1.7.3): Ungroups the given groups one level, like Edit > Grouping > Ungroup: each group is dissolved, the elements and subgroups it directly contains stay. A group nested in another group is reported as failed; ungroup the containing group first. Returns an execution result per group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetGroupsOfElements** (since 1.5.6): Gets the identifier of the group that directly contains each given element. Returns an error for elements that are not part of any group. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementsOfGroups** (since 1.5.6): Gets the elements directly contained by each given group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetMainGroups** (since 1.8.0): Gets the top level group of each given group. A group that is not nested in another group is its own top level group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetAllElementsOfGroups** (since 1.8.0): Gets all the elements of each given group, including the elements of its nested groups. Parameters: groups.
- **GetAutoGroupMode** (since 1.8.0): Gets the current state of the Auto Group mode.
- **GetElementSetData** (since 1.8.0): Gets the elements and the custom data of each given element set. Element sets are created by add-ons to link elements together; the custom data is returned as Base64 encoded bytes. Parameters: elementSets.
- **GetUserDataOfGroups** (since 1.7.3): Gets the user data an add-on attached to each given group: its version, platform sign, flags and bytes (base64 encoded), and, when its version is 1 (the layout SetUserDataOfGroups writes), its key-value pairs. Returns an error for groups that have no user data. Parameters: groups.
- **SetUserDataOfGroups** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys in the user data of groups, for scripts to keep their own state on a group. The given pairs are merged into what each group already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. One undo step per call. Parameters: groups, pairs, keysToDelete.
- **GetSuspendGroupsMode** (since 1.5.6): Gets the current state of the Suspend Groups mode.
- **SetSuspendGroupsMode** (since 1.5.6): Turns the Suspend Groups mode on or off. Suspend groups to perform operations on elements that are part of a group; remember to restore the previous state afterwards. Parameters: suspendGroups.
- **CreateElementSets** (since 1.8.0): Creates element sets of the given elements. An element set is a hidden, persistent collection of elements (it is not a group and has no effect on selection or editing). Parameters: elementSets.
- **DeleteElementSets** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the given element sets. The elements of a set are not deleted. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On can be deleted; sets created by other add-ons are reported as failed. Parameters: elementSets.
- **GetElementSetsOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the element sets that contain each given element. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On are examined; sets created by other add-ons are not found. Parameters: elements.

## Favorites Commands

- **GetFavoritesByType** (since 1.2.2): Returns a list of the names of all favorites with the given element type Parameters: elementType.
- **GetAllFavorites** (since 1.7.3): Returns every Favorite of the project, or only those of the given element type, with its name and element type. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elementType.
- **GetFavoritePreviewImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the preview image of the given favorite. Parameters: favorite, imageType, format, width, height.
- **GetFavoriteDetails** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classifications, property values and element category values stored in the given favorites, so they can be audited before elements are placed. Each property value comes with its evaluation status and default-value flag; the value itself is only returned when it has been evaluated. Parameters: favorites.
- **ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults** (since 1.1.2): Apply the given favorites to element defaults. Parameters: favorites.
- **CreateFavoritesFromElements** (since 1.1.2): Create favorites from the given elements. Parameters: favoritesFromElements.
- **ImportFavorites** (since 1.5.0): Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew. Parameters: path, format, fileNames, targetFolder, importFolders, conflictPolicy.
- **ExportFavorites** (since 1.5.0): Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format). Parameters: path, names, format.
- **ApplyFavoritesToElements** (since 1.5.4): Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. Parameters: favoritesToApply, applySettings, applyClassifications, applyCategories, applyProperties, keepFields.
- **UpdateFavoritesFromElements** (since 1.5.4): Update existing favorites from the given elements. Parameters: favoritesFromElements.
- **RenameFavorites** (since 1.5.4): Rename existing favorites. Parameters: renames.
- **DeleteFavorites** (since 1.5.4): Delete existing favorites. Parameters: favorites.
- **GetFavoriteFolders** (since 1.8.0): Returns the folder tree of the Favorites palette from its root folder: the name and path of every folder and the names of the Favorites in it. Available from Archicad 29.
- **CreateFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Creates a folder in the Favorites palette, in the parent folder given by its path. Returns the new folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: parentPath, name.
- **RenameFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Renames a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. The root folder cannot be renamed. Returns the renamed folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: path, newName.
- **DeleteFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Deletes a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Archicad deletes the folder's Favorites and subfolders with it, so a folder that is not empty is deleted only if recursive is true. The root folder cannot be deleted. Returns the deleted folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: path, recursive.
- **GetFavoriteSettings** (since 1.7.3): Reads the stored settings of the given favorites without applying them or placing an element: the element type, the folder, the library part and GDL parameters, the marker (library part and parameters) of Window and Door favorites, and the sub-elements. A favorite without a marker has no marker field, which is not an error. The other settings of the element (pens, layer, structure, etc.) are not returned. Parameters: favorites.
- **CreateFavorite** (since 1.8.0): Creates a Favorite in the given folder from the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. conflictPolicy says what happens when the name is taken: fail, skip, overwrite the existing Favorite's settings or create the new one under a free name. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: name, folder, source, conflictPolicy.
- **ChangeFavorite** (since 1.8.0): Gives an existing Favorite the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favoriteName, source.
- **ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault** (since 1.8.0): Makes the settings of the given Favorite the settings of its tool, and returns the element type of that tool. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favoriteName.
- **MoveFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Moves a folder of the Favorites palette, with its Favorites and subfolders, into another folder. Folders are given as their path of folder names from the root. Returns the new path of the folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: folder, targetFolder.
- **MoveFavorites** (since 1.8.0): Moves Favorites given by their names into a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Returns an execution result for each Favorite. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favorites, targetPath.

## Property Commands

- **GetAllProperties** (since 1.1.3): Returns all user defined and built-in properties. Optionally only the given properties or property types, and without the availability lists. Parameters: properties, propertyTypes, includeAvailability.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfElements** (since 1.0.6): Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element. Parameters: elements, properties, includeAvailability.
- **SetPropertyValuesOfElements** (since 1.0.6): Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. Parameters: elementPropertyValues.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.1.8): Returns the property values of the attributes for the given property. With includeStatus it also returns whether each property is available, editable and visible for the attribute (from 1.7.3). Parameters: attributeIds, properties, includeStatus.
- **SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.1.8): Sets the property values of attributes. Parameters: attributePropertyValues.
- **SetBuiltInPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Sets built-in property values of attributes, writing the values of each attribute together. Custom properties are refused; set them with SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes. Returns one execution result per value. Parameters: attributes.
- **GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Returns the property definitions of the given attributes (for example Building Materials): the user defined, the fundamental built-in, or all of them. Parameters: attributeIds, filter.
- **GetPropertiesOfToolDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Returns the property definitions of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types, filtered by kind (all by default), and optionally the value of each property in the tool default. Parameters: elementTypes, filter, includeValues.
- **AddPropertyToAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only. Parameters: propertyId, attributeIds.
- **RemovePropertyFromAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Makes a custom property unavailable for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only. Parameters: propertyId, attributeIds.
- **CreatePropertyGroups** (since 1.0.7): Creates Property Groups based on the given parameters. Parameters: propertyGroups.
- **DeletePropertyGroups** (since 1.0.9): Deletes the given Custom Property Groups. Parameters: propertyGroupIds.
- **CreatePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.0.9): Creates Custom Property Definitions based on the given parameters. Parameters: propertyDefinitions.
- **DeletePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.0.9): Deletes the given Custom Property Definitions. Parameters: propertyIds.
- **UpdatePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.5.4): Updates existing Custom Property Definitions in place, keeping their guid: name, description, group, default value or expressions, availability, and enum options (add, rename, remove, reorder). Parameters: propertyDefinitions.
- **UpdatePropertyGroups** (since 1.6.0): Updates the name and/or description of existing Custom Property Groups, keeping their guid. Parameters: propertyGroups.
- **ImportPropertiesXml** (since 1.6.0): Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed. Parameters: xml, conflictPolicy.
- **ModifyPropertyValueOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets one property value on all the given elements in a single step. If the property is not available for any of the elements, none of them is changed. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements, propertyId, propertyValue.
- **GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the given properties are available and whether they are visible in the current tool default of an element type, before creating new elements. It checks the native tool default only, not a Favorite that is not applied. Unknown properties are reported as errors, not as unavailable. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: elementType, properties.
- **MakePropertyAvailableForElements** (since 1.7.3): Makes a property definition available for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27. Parameters: elements, propertyId.
- **MakePropertyUnavailableForElements** (since 1.7.3): Makes a property definition unavailable for all the given elements. Available only in Archicad 27. Parameters: elements, propertyId.

## Classification Commands

- **GetClassificationsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Returns the classification of the given elements in the given classification systems. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. Parameters: elements, classificationSystemIds.
- **GetElementsByClassification** (since 1.8.0): Returns the elements classified with the given classification items, one list per item, so elements can be filtered by classification in a single call. Parameters: classificationItemIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. Parameters: elementClassifications.
- **GetClassificationsOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classifications of the given attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.) in every classification system they are classified in. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Sets the classifications of attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.). The given item replaces the attribute's current item in the same classification system. In order to set the classification of an attribute to unclassified in a system, omit the classificationItemId field. Parameters: attributeClassifications.
- **GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classification of the given attributes (for example Building Materials) in the given classification system. classificationItemId is omitted for an unclassified attribute. Parameters: attributeIds, classificationSystemId.
- **GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults** (since 1.7.3): Returns the classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types in the given classification systems. Parameters: elementTypes, classificationSystemIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults** (since 1.7.3): Sets the classifications of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types. In order to set a default to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. Parameters: elementDefaultClassifications.
- **GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Returns every classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types, in all classification systems at once. Unlike GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults it needs no list of classification systems; systems in which a default is unclassified are left out. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **GetAllClassificationSystems** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classification systems of the project with their guid, name, description, source, version and date. Same output as the official GetAllClassificationSystems command, so scripts can rely on Tapir commands only.
- **CreateClassificationSystems** (since 1.5.0): Creates Classification Systems including Classification Items based on the given parameters. Parameters: classificationSystemsWithItems.
- **CreateClassificationItems** (since 1.5.0): Creates Classification Items in the given Classification Systems based on the given parameters. Parameters: newClassificationItems.
- **DeleteClassificationSystems** (since 1.5.2): Deletes the given Classification Systems. Parameters: classificationSystemIds.
- **DeleteClassificationItems** (since 1.5.2): Deletes the given Classification Items. Parameters: classificationItemIds.
- **UpdateClassificationSystems** (since 1.6.0): Updates the name, description, source, version and/or date of existing Classification Systems, keeping their guid. Parameters: classificationSystems.
- **UpdateClassificationItems** (since 1.6.0): Updates the id (code), name and/or description of existing Classification Items, keeping their guid and so the elements classified with them. Items cannot be moved to another parent. Parameters: classificationItems.
- **GetClassificationItemParents** (since 1.8.0): Returns the parent item and the classification system of the given Classification Items; a top level item has no parent. The output is aligned with the input array of items. Parameters: classificationItemIds.
- **ImportClassificationsXml** (since 1.6.0): Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed. Parameters: xml, systemConflictPolicy, itemConflictPolicy.
- **GetClassificationItemVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the given classification items are visible (offered) for the given elements, element tool defaults and attributes, such as building materials. Non-existing targets and classification items are reported as errors. Visibility does not tell whether the target is classified with the item, and an item can be visible even if its parent item is not. Parameters: targets, classificationItemIds.

## Attribute Commands

- **GetAttributesByType** (since 1.1.3): Returns the details of every attribute of the given type. From Archicad 30 an attribute that Archicad keeps a creation record of also carries creationInfo: how (method), from where (source), by whom and when it was created. Parameters: attributeType.
- **GetAttributesFromProject** (since 1.7.3): Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Archicad does not read Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem attributes from a file that is not open: these types get an error item instead of an empty list. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: projectFilePath, attributeTypes.
- **DeleteAttributes** (since 1.5.4): Deletes the given attributes. Parameters: attributesToDelete.
- **GetUsedAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Gets the attributes in use, as Archicad reports them for the usedAttributes JSON query: parsed into usedAttributes when the report is a JSON object, otherwise as text in raw. Helps to find the attributes DeleteAttributes can remove before a handover. Available from Archicad 27.
- **ConsolidateLines** (since 1.8.0): Runs the Line Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
- **ConsolidateFills** (since 1.8.0): Runs the Fill Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
- **CreateAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Creates attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path (the folder names from the root folder down). Missing parent folders are created too; a folder that already exists is kept and reported as success. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders.
- **DeleteAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Deletes attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, together with all the subfolders and deletable attributes they contain (a folder holding an attribute that cannot be deleted is kept). The root folder cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders.
- **RenameAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Renames attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, to the given new names. The root folder cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders.
- **MoveAttributesAndFolders** (since 1.7.3): Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeIds, attributeFolders, targetFolder.
- **CreateLayers** (since 1.0.3): Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: layerDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateLayerCombinations** (since 1.2.4): Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: layerCombinationDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateLines** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: lineDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateFills** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Fill attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: fillDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateZoneCategories** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Zone Category attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: zoneCategoryDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateMEPSystems** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface) based on the given parameters. Parameters: mepSystemDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreatePenTables** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: penTableDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **ModifyPens** (since 1.7.2): Changes the color, width and description of single pens of the Pen Table in effect for the model views (the default) or the layouts, keeping every other pen as it is. Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet). Parameters: pens, target.
- **CreateProfiles** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters. Parameters: profileDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateBuildingMaterials** (since 1.0.1): Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: buildingMaterialDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateComposites** (since 1.0.2): Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: compositeDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateSurfaces** (since 1.2.2): Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: surfaceDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **GetBuildingMaterialPhysicalProperties** (since 0.1.3): Retrieves the physical properties of the given Building Materials. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **GetLayerCombinations** (since 1.2.4): Returns the details of layer combination attributes. Parameters: attributes.
- **GetCurrentLayerCombination** (since 1.7.3): Returns the layer combination in effect in the current window. No layer combination is returned when the current state of the layers matches none.
- **GetLines** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Line attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetFills** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Fill attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetZoneCategories** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Zone Category attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetMEPSystems** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface). Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetPenTables** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Pen Table attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetCurrentPenTable** (since 1.7.3): Returns the current Pen Table (its index, attribute identifier and name) and its number of pens. Pass the returned attributeId to GetPenTables to read the pens.
- **GetPens** (since 1.8.0): Returns the given pens, or all of them, in effect in the current window: index, color, width and description. It also works when the pens in effect are not a Pen Table attribute. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: indices.
- **GetProfiles** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Profile attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetComposites** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Composite attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetSurfaces** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Surface attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetLayers** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Layer attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetBuildingMaterials** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Building Material attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetFontsByName** (since 1.7.3): Finds loaded fonts by name through Archicad's font search and returns their index (as Text and Label fields reference fonts in fontIndex) and name, or an error for a name no loaded font has. Parameters: fontNames.
- **GetGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override rules of the project, with their rule group, criterion and style. Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName** (since 1.7.3): Gets graphic override rules by name, with their rule group, criterion and style. The rule group narrows the search; without it the rule is searched in every rule group. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **ModifyGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override rules. They are also removed from the combinations that contain them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRuleIds.
- **GetGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override combinations of the project with the rules they contain. Available from Archicad 27.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Creates graphic override combinations from existing rules. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinations.
- **ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the name and/or the rules of graphic override combinations. Omitted fields are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinations.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override combinations. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinationIds.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.8.0): Creates empty graphic override rule groups. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames.
- **GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override rule groups of the project with the rules they contain, empty groups included. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder** (since 1.8.0): Sets the order of the rules in graphic override rule groups, found by name. The listed rules come first, in the given order; the other rules of the group keep their order after them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRuleGroups.
- **RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.3): Renames graphic override rule groups, found by name. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroups.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override rule groups, found by name. A group that still contains rules is kept unless its rules are moved to another group or deleted with it. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames, moveRulesToGroup, deleteRules.
- **SetGraphicOverrideRuleGroupOrder** (since 1.8.0): Sets the order of the graphic override rule groups, found by name. The groups not listed keep their order and follow the listed ones. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames.
- **MoveGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.3): Moves graphic override rules to another rule group, or to another place in their own group. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **GetUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Reads the key-value pairs stored on attributes by SetUserDataOfAttributes. An attribute without user data returns no pairs; one holding user data in another layout returns an error. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **SetUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys in the user data of attributes, for scripts to keep their own state on an attribute. The given pairs are merged into what each attribute already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. Parameters: attributeIds, pairs, keysToDelete.
- **DeleteUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Removes the user data of attributes, every key at once. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. Parameters: attributeIds.

## IFC Commands

- **IFCFileOperation** (since 1.2.6): Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use. Parameters: method, ifcFilePath, fileType, translatorName, elementsToExport.
- **GetIFCExportTranslators** (since 1.6.0): Lists the IFC export translators of the project, the preview translator first. Pass one of the names to IFCFileOperation as translatorName.
- **GetElementsByIFCIds** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the elements by the given IFC identifiers. Accepts IFC GlobalIds in every Archicad version. Parameters: ifcIds.
- **GetIFCIdsOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC identifiers of the given elements. Before Archicad 28 it also returns their IFC GlobalIds. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCTypeOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC types of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC properties of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCAttributesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType, LongName, ...) of the given elements, subelements included: the name, the IFC value type and the value of each attribute. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 storedOnly returns only the attributes stored on the elements. Parameters: elements, storedOnly.
- **SetIFCAttributesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Sets the values of IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of elements. The attribute must be one GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element; its IFC value type is kept. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCAttributeValues.
- **SetIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.7.0): Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCPropertyValues.
- **GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the IFC classification references of the given elements, subelements included: identification, name, location, description (from Archicad 29), the referenced classification (name, source, edition) and whether the reference comes from the preview translator or is stored locally. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 the source is not given, the referenced classification also has its edition date, description and location, and storedOnly returns only the references stored on the elements. Parameters: elements, storedOnly.
- **SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Stores IFC classification references (identification, name, location and the referenced classification with its name, edition, edition date, description and location) on elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCClassificationReferences.
- **RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Removes IFC classification references stored on elements, given by the name of their classification and optionally their identification; without identification every stored reference of that classification is removed. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCClassificationReferences.
- **RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Removes local IFC properties, given by property set and property name, from elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCProperties.

## Library Commands

- **GetLibraries** (since 1.0.1): Gets the list of loaded libraries. From Archicad 28 a library package also gets its package information (ID, versions, minimum Archicad version and dependencies).
- **ReloadLibraries** (since 1.0.0): Executes the reload libraries command.
- **AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.2.2): Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer). Parameters: files, overwriteExisting.
- **DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems** (since 1.6.0): Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: embeddedLibraryItems.
- **CreateLibraryParts** (since 1.8.0): Creates GDL library parts in the embedded library from their scripts (master, 2D, 3D, parameter, interface, properties) and parameter definitions, under the given parent subtype. The new parts are placeable right away, e.g. with CreateObjects. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new part is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer). Parameters: libraryParts, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.7.3): Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary. Parameters: folderPath.
- **CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.7.3): Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced. Parameters: files, targetFolder, overwriteIfExists.
- **SetLibraries** (since 1.5.9): Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear. Parameters: libraries.
- **AddLibraries** (since 1.5.9): Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded. Parameters: libraries.
- **GetAvailableLibraryParts** (since 1.5.0): Lists library parts currently available to the project. Filter by typeId (e.g. 'Door', 'Window', 'Object', 'Lamp'). Parameters: filterByTypeId.
- **GetLibraryPartOriginalLocations** (since 1.8.0): Gets the original location of the given library parts, the file they came from, e.g. before they were embedded into the project. The library parts are given by the index GetAvailableLibraryParts returns. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **IsUsableGDLString** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether each of the given strings is usable in GDL, e.g. before writing it into a GDL parameter or script. Returns one boolean for each string. Parameters: strings.
- **CheckLibraries** (since 1.8.0): Checks the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library check. Returns the error the API reports, if any.
- **ResetLibraries** (since 1.8.0): Resets the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library reset.
- **SetLibraryPartScripts** (since 1.7.3): Sets and deletes the master, parameter, 2D, 3D, properties, interface and forward and backward migration scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty, deleteScripts removes it. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **SetLibraryPartMetadata** (since 1.8.0): Sets the author, keywords, license, license version, password and the placeable, UI default, subtype and hierarchical pages flags of loaded library parts. Only the given fields are changed. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartPictures** (since 1.8.0): Gets the preview picture and the GDL pictures of a loaded library part as base64 encoded PNGs, and from Archicad 29 also their dark user interface variants. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name.
- **SetLibraryPartPictures** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the preview picture, the GDL pictures (and from Archicad 29 their dark variants) or the 2D symbol of a loaded library part, or copies the 2D symbol from another library part. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, deletePreviewPicture, deleteDarkPreviewPicture, deleteGdlPictures, deleteDarkGdlPictures, copy2DSymbolFrom, delete2DSymbol.
- **GetLibraryPartCustomSection** (since 1.8.0): Gets a custom section of a loaded library part by its section identifier and index: whether it exists, its data version and its content as base64. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, sectionId, index.
- **SetLibraryPartCustomSection** (since 1.8.0): Creates, replaces or deletes a custom section of a loaded library part. The content is given as base64. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, sectionId, index, dataVersion, data, delete.
- **CreateLibraryPart** (since 1.8.0): Creates a new library part file (.gsm) of the given loaded subtype, inheriting its parameters, and reports whether it is loaded with its index and names. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: path, ancestorSubtype.
- **OpenLibraryPartInEditor** (since 1.8.0): Opens a loaded library part, given by its fileName or documentName as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts, in Archicad's library part editor. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.

## Teamwork Commands

- **TeamworkSend** (since 0.1.0): Performs a send operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
- **TeamworkReceive** (since 0.1.0): Performs a receive operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
- **GetTeamworkProjectInfo** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and whether it is online, and returns its BIMcloud server, project name and the current user (id and name).
- **ReserveElements** (since 1.1.4): Reserves elements in Teamwork mode. Parameters: elements.
- **ReleaseElements** (since 1.1.4): Releases elements in Teamwork mode. Parameters: elements.
- **GetReservationStatusOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Returns the Teamwork reservation status of elements without reserving them: whether each element is free, reserved by the current user or reserved by another user, with the reserving user and the element's owner. Parameters: elements.
- **GrantElements** (since 1.7.3): Hands over the reservation of elements to another Teamwork user, given by user id, without a dialog. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements, userId.
- **ReserveLockableObjectSet** (since 1.7.1): Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **ReleaseLockableObjectSet** (since 1.7.1): Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **GetLockableObjectSetStatus** (since 1.7.1): Returns the Teamwork reservation status of a non-element lockable object set and the users who hold it. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement** (since 1.7.1): Reserves the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode, which is needed before changing hotlink nodes.
- **ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement** (since 1.7.1): Releases the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode.
- **GetTeamworkStatus** (since 1.7.3): Returns whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and is online, the members of the shared project and who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Works in a solo project too, then isShared and isOnline are false.
- **GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases** (since 1.8.0): Returns the Teamwork owner (user id and name) of each given database, e.g. of a layout or a view database. The user id is 0 when nobody owns the database. Parameters: databases.
- **UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud** (since 1.8.0): Uploads local library folders or container files (.lcf) to a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server, as BIMcloud libraries. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: libraryPaths, serverUrl, parentPath.
- **RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud** (since 1.8.0): Removes libraries, given by name, from a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: libraryNames, serverUrl, parentPath.

## Navigator Commands

- **PublishPublisherSet** (since 0.1.0): Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published. Parameters: publisherSetName, outputPath, selectedNavigatorItemIds.
- **UpdateDrawings** (since 1.1.4): Performs a drawing update on the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDrawingContentBoxes** (since 1.7.3): Returns the full content box of the given Drawing elements, independent of their frames, as ACAPI_Drawing_GetFullDrawingContentBox reports it. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId** (since 1.1.4): Gets the ID of the database associated with the supplied navigator item id Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **GetDatabases** (since 1.7.3): Lists every database of the given types (sections, elevations, interior elevations, details, worksheets, 3D documents, layouts, master layouts) with its database ID, name and reference ID, without walking the navigator trees. Parameters: types.
- **CreateDetails** (since 1.4.0): Creates independent Detail databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new detail. Parameters: detailsData.
- **CreateWorksheets** (since 1.4.0): Creates independent Worksheet databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new worksheet. Parameters: worksheetsData.
- **CreateLayout** (since 1.4.0): Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. Parameters: layoutsData.
- **CreateLayoutSubset** (since 1.4.0): Creates Layout Book subsets. Parameters: subsetsData.
- **GetLayoutSubsetSettings** (since 1.7.3): Gets the settings of existing Layout Book subsets: the same fields CreateLayoutSubset accepts (name, ID prefix, numbering style, ...). Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **CreateDrawings** (since 1.4.0): Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items. Parameters: drawingsData.
- **ChangeDrawingLink** (since 1.5.7): Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored. Parameters: drawingsWithNewLinks.
- **GetLayoutSettings** (since 1.1.7): Gets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. Parameters: layoutDatabaseIds.
- **SetLayoutSettings** (since 1.1.7): Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. Parameters: layoutsData.
