- **GetLayoutCustomScheme** (since 1.1.7): Gets the Layout Info Panel custom field definitions (name and key) from Book Settings.
- **GetDrawingNumberingGridLines** (since 1.8.0): Gets the lines of the grid of the grid-based drawing numbering of the current layout (start and end point, pen index, line type index), for example to find which grid cell a drawing on the layout sits in. The current window must be a layout (see ChangeWindow), and only a layout that uses grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.
- **GetModelViewOptions** (since 1.1.4): Gets all model view options
- **FindModelViewOption** (since 1.8.0): Finds a model view option combination by id or by name and returns its index, id, name and flags. The index is the one Archicad uses to switch the model view options of a window to the combination. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: modelViewOptionId, name.
- **GetViewOptions** (since 1.8.0): Gets the model view options and on-screen view options of the current plan window, and the index of the model view option combination it applies.
- **SetViewOptions** (since 1.8.0): Switches the current plan window to a model view option combination by index, and/or changes the given model view options and on-screen view options. Parameters: modelViewOptionIndex, viewOptions.
- **GetViewSettings** (since 1.1.4): Gets the view settings of navigator items Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **SetViewSettings** (since 1.1.4): Sets the view settings of navigator items Parameters: navigatorItemIdsWithViewSettings.
- **GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.
- **SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: combinationId, name.
- **GetRenovationFilters** (since 1.8.0): Gets the renovation filters of the project, and the one the current window uses (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter). A renovationFilterId has the same shape as the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings, so a filter listed here can be set on saved views too.
- **SetActiveRenovationFilter** (since 1.8.0): Sets the renovation filter of the current window (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter), given by its renovationFilterId from GetRenovationFilters or by its name. Saved views keep their own filter: change that with SetViewSettings. Parameters: renovationFilterId, name.
- **GetGhostStorySettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the Trace & Reference ghost story settings of the floor plan: whether it is on, whether one story, the story above or the one below is shown, which story, its color and the element types shown in it.
- **SetGhostStorySettings** (since 1.8.0): Sets the Trace & Reference ghost story settings of the floor plan through its ghost record, which is created when the floor plan has none. Every field is optional; the ones left out keep their value, and without a story choice the current reference is kept. Parameters: on, showOne, showAbove, showBelow, storyIndex, ghostColor, filter.
- **GetStructureDisplay** (since 1.7.3): Gets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, and whether it is the 3D window. This is the setting of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetStructureDisplay** (since 1.7.3): Sets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, e.g. the floor plan, a section or the 3D window. The change cannot be undone. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: structureDisplay.
- **GetView2DTransformations** (since 1.1.7): Get zoom and rotation of 2D views Parameters: navigatorItemIds, databases.
- **SetViewRotation** (since 1.1.7): Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database. Parameters: navigatorItemIdsWithRotation.
- **CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap** (since 1.1.7): Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder. Parameters: viewsData.
- **CreateViewsInViewMap** (since 1.1.7): Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items. Parameters: viewsData.
- **CreateViewMapFolder** (since 1.1.7): Creates a new folder in the View Map. Parameters: folderName, parentNavigatorItemId.
- **Set3DCutPlanes** (since 1.3.1): Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off. Parameters: cutPlanes.
- **Get3DCutPlanes** (since 1.7.3): Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on and the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.
- **Get3DStyleDetails** (since 1.7.3): Gets the settings of 3D styles by name (an empty name or no names means the current 3D style): rendering engine, model type, monochrome and background colors, contours, shadows and hatching. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: names.
- **Create3DStyles** (since 1.7.3): Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: styles.
- **Change3DStyles** (since 1.7.3): Changes the given fields of existing 3D styles, identified by name. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: styles.
- **Get3DProjectionSettings** (since 1.7.2): Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the transformation matrix of an axonometry.
- **Set3DProjectionSettings** (since 1.7.2): Sets a perspective projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. Parameters: perspective.
- **GetDocumentFrom3DDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Gets the defaults a newly created 3D Document starts with: name, reference ID, vectorial hatching and sun shadows, transparency, connection to the model, surfaces, boundary contours and the uniform cut, uncut, shadow and hidden edge attributes.
- **SetDocumentFrom3DDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Sets the defaults a newly created 3D Document starts with. Only the given fields are changed; existing 3D Documents are not affected. The fields are the ones returned by GetDocumentFrom3DDefaults. Parameters: name, refId, vect3DHatching, vectSunShadow, mustBeTransparent, intPlanConn, materialFrom3D, contureOff, cMater, boundaryDisplay, boundaryPen, boundaryLineType, attributeOptions.
- **Get3DWindowSettings** (since 1.7.3): Gets the 3D window settings: the pixel size of the 3D window and the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection.
- **Set3DWindowSettings** (since 1.7.3): Changes the pixel size of the 3D window and/or the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection; the values not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Archicad may need a rebuild of the 3D window (RebuildView) before it shows the change, e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage. Parameters: hSize, vSize, zoomScaleX, zoomScaleY, zoomDispX, zoomDispY.
- **Get3DFilterAndCutSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window: the stories shown, the filter mode and which element types are shown. Available from Archicad 27.
- **Set3DFilterAndCutSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window; only the given fields and the listed element types change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: settings, rebuild.
- **GetGridSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window, and which database that is. Each database has its own grid settings. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGridSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window; only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: settings.
- **FitInWindow** (since 1.3.1): Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window. Parameters: elements.
- **ZoomToElements** (since 1.8.0): Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer. Parameters: elements, keepSelection.
- **SetZoom** (since 1.7.3): Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates. Parameters: zoomBox.
- **ResetZoom** (since 1.7.3): Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back. Parameters: numberOfStepsBack.
- **CreateSections** (since 1.5.0): Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back. Parameters: sectionsData.
- **CreateInteriorElevations** (since 1.5.8): Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room. Parameters: interiorElevationsData.
- **MoveNavigatorItem** (since 1.1.7): Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to. Parameters: navigatorItemIdToMove, parentNavigatorItemId, previousNavigatorItemId.
- **RenameNavigatorItem** (since 1.1.7): Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again. Parameters: navigatorItemId, newName, newId, customName.
- **DeleteNavigatorItems** (since 1.1.7): Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **GetNavigatorItemTree** (since 1.1.7): Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children. Parameters: navigatorMapId, publisherSetName, includeChildCount.
- **GetNavigatorParentItems** (since 1.7.3): Returns the parent of each given navigator item: the folder, subset or layout book item it is in. The root of a map has no parent and gets an error. Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **SetMasterLayoutContext** (since 1.8.0): Sets which layout's context the master layout of the current window is drawn in: its autotexts then show the values of the given layout. The current window must be a master layout, otherwise an error is returned. It does not assign a master layout to a layout. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: layoutDatabaseId.
- **GetAddOnViewpointRoots** (since 1.8.0): Returns the roots of the add-on viewpoints: the Project Map items created through the Archicad API by an add-on, as Archicad lists them to Tapir. Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetAddOnViewpointChildren** (since 1.8.0): Returns the direct children of an add-on viewpoint root or group. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpointId.
- **GetAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Returns the details of the given add-on viewpoint items: their parent, type (Root, Group or Leaf), ID, name, view settings flags and attached data (base64 encoded). The output is aligned with the input array; an item that cannot be read gets an error. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpointIds.
- **CreateAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpoints.
- **ChangeAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Changes the ID, name, view settings flags or attached data (base64 encoded) of the given add-on viewpoint items; only the given fields are changed. Roots and groups can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpoints.

## Graphic Override Commands

- **CreateGraphicalOverrideRule** (since 1.7.2): Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: name, ruleGroupName, criterionXML, surfaceRGB, linePenIndex, overrideContours.
- **GetGraphicalOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.
- **CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: name, ruleNames.
- **GetGraphicalOverrideStyleOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Returns the graphic override style each element is drawn with in the current window: for every overridable member (line type, pens, fill types, surfaces, ...) whether the active graphic override combination replaces it, and with what. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elements.

## Issue Management Commands

- **CreateIssue** (since 1.0.2): Creates a new issue. Parameters: name, parentIssueId, tagText.
- **DeleteIssue** (since 1.0.2): Deletes the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, acceptAllElements.
- **GetIssues** (since 1.0.2): Retrieves information about existing issues.
- **AddCommentToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Adds a new comment to the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, author, status, text.
- **GetCommentsFromIssue** (since 1.0.6): Retrieves comments information from the specified issue. Parameters: issueId.
- **AttachElementsToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Attaches elements to the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, elements, type.
- **DetachElementsFromIssue** (since 1.0.6): Detaches elements from the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, elements.
- **GetElementsAttachedToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Retrieves attached elements of the specified issue, filtered by attachment type. Parameters: issueId, type.
- **ExportIssuesToBCF** (since 1.0.6): Exports specified issues to a BCF file. Parameters: issues, exportPath, useExternalId, alignBySurveyPoint.
- **ImportIssuesFromBCF** (since 1.0.6): Imports issues from the specified BCF file. Parameters: importPath, alignBySurveyPoint.
- **ImportMarkupsFromPDF** (since 1.7.3): Imports the markups of the specified PDF file as issues, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups, without any dialog and without opening the Issue Manager palette, and reports the issues it created. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: pdfFilePath.

## Revision Management Commands

- **GetRevisionIssues** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all issues.
- **ModifyRevisionIssues** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the ID, the short description and the custom scheme data of the given revision issues. Only the given fields are changed. Issued revision issues may refuse the change. Parameters: revisionIssues.
- **GetRevisionChanges** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all changes.
- **GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the custom fields of changes (the change custom scheme): the key and the name of each field. The keys are the customSchemeKey values in the customSchemeData of changes.
- **GetDocumentRevisions** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all document revisions.
- **GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all changes belong to the last revision of the given layouts. Parameters: layoutDatabaseIds.
- **GetRevisionChangesOfElements** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves the changes belong to the given elements. Parameters: elements.

## Design Options Commands

- **GetDesignOptions** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design options. Available from Archicad 29.
- **GetDesignOptionSets** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design option sets, and in Teamwork projects the Teamwork identifier of the design options. Available from Archicad 29.
- **GetDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design option combinations.
- **GetElementsOfDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the elements associated with the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **GetDesignOptionForElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the design option association for the specified elements. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateDesignOptionSets** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **CreateDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **CreateDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.5.1): Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: activeDesignOptionsInCombinations.
- **ActivateDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Activates one design option in each of the given combinations, without listing all active design options of the combination. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionsToActivate.
- **DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.7.3): Turns off the given design options in the given combinations, leaving their other options as they are. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: deactivatedDesignOptionsInCombinations.
- **MoveElementsToDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elementDesignOptionPairs.
- **MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet** (since 1.5.1): Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionAndSetPairs.
- **RenameDesignOptions** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **RenameDesignOptionSets** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **RenameDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **DeleteDesignOptions** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **DeleteDesignOptionSets** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **DeleteDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **SetDefaultDesignOption** (since 1.8.0): Sets the given design option as the default, or the Main Model when no design option is given. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionId.
- **ReorderDesignOptionSets** (since 1.8.0): Moves the given design option sets before another set or to the end of the list. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **ReorderDesignOptionsInSet** (since 1.8.0): Moves the given design options before another design option of the same set or to the end of their set. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **CanMoveElementsToDesignOptions** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether the given elements can be moved to another design option or to the main model, with the reason when they cannot. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.3): Duplicates the given design option combinations and returns the identifiers of the new combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **GetHotlinkDesignOptionTableDetails** (since 1.8.0): Reads the design option table of hotlink nodes: the design option sets, options and combinations of the hotlinked source file, and which of them the node shows. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.

## Keynote Commands

- **GetKeynoteTree** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the whole keynote folder and item hierarchy. The technical root folder is not included in the output; the top-level folders and items are returned directly. Available from Archicad 28.
- **GetKeynoteAutoTexts** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the autotext tokens of the given keynote items. The tokens can be used as label text content to reference the fields of a keynote item. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteItems.
- **CreateKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: foldersData.
- **CreateKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: itemsData.
- **ModifyKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: foldersData.
- **ModifyKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: itemsData.
- **DeleteKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteFolderIds.
- **DeleteKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteItemIds.
- **CreateKeynoteLabels** (since 1.5.6): Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: labelsData.

## Project Data Commands

- **GetProjectDataKeys** (since 1.7.3): Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.
- **GetProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Gets the content of the project data with the given names. Parameters: names.
- **SetProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data. Parameters: values.
- **DeleteProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Deletes the project data with the given names. Parameters: names.
- **ReserveProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it. Parameters: names.
- **ReleaseProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork. Parameters: names.
- **RequestProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message. Parameters: names, mailText.
- **GrantProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user. Parameters: names, toUserId.

## MEP Commands

- **GetMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elementTypes, domains.
- **GetMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetMEPPorts** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetMEPDistributionSystems** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.
- **CreateMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: routingElementsData.
- **CreateMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with a changed insulation that applies only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elementsData.
- **ModifyMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, and node positions. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: routingElementsData.
- **ModifyMEPPorts** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: portsData.
- **ConnectMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: connectionsData.
- **CheckMEPPortConnectability** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: portPairs.
- **GetMEPPreferenceTables** (since 1.5.7): Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: domain, includeFittingTables.
- **ModifyMEPPreferenceTables** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, and deletes reference ids from the reference set and angles from the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: domain, tablesToAdd, tables, tablesToDelete, referenceIdsToDelete, anglesToDelete.
- **GetMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.2): Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.
- **CreateMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.2): Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: systemGroupsData.
- **CreateMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.2): Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystemsData.
- **ModifyMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.3): Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: systemGroupsData.
- **ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.3): Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystemsData.
- **DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.3): Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystems.
- **GetMEPRoutingParameters** (since 1.8.0): Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **SetMEPRoutingParameters** (since 1.8.0): Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElectricalPanels** (since 1.7.2): Gets the electrical panels (distribution boards) of the project or the given ones: name, circuit naming, circuits, parent circuit, placement and the connected and demand loads in total and per phase. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElectricalCircuits** (since 1.7.2): Gets the given electrical circuits, the circuits of the given panels, or every circuit of the project: name, description, owner panel, connected devices and panels, voltage, phases, wiring type, loads, voltage drop and estimated cable length. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: elements, electricalPanels.
- **GetElectricalDevices** (since 1.7.2): Gets the electrical devices (lights, sockets and other consumers) of the project or the given ones: parent circuit, placement, apparent power, load classification, demand load and directly connected MEP elements. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElectricalProjectSettings** (since 1.7.2): Gets the electrical project settings: the default voltage, the wiring types with their cross-sectional area and the load classifications with their demand factor. Available from Archicad 30.
- **CreateElectricalPanels** (since 1.7.2): Places electrical panels with the default settings of the Electrical Panel tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, panel name and circuit naming. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalPanelsData.
- **CreateElectricalDevices** (since 1.7.2): Places electrical devices with the default settings of the Electrical Device tool, optionally with the given library part, size, rotation, mirroring, apparent power and load classification, and connects them to a circuit. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalDevicesData.
- **ModifyElectricalPanels** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the name, circuit naming and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical panels. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalPanelsData.
- **CreateElectricalCircuits** (since 1.7.2): Adds new circuits to electrical panels, optionally with the given description, voltage, wiring type and used phases. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalCircuitsData.
- **DeleteElectricalCircuits** (since 1.7.2): Removes electrical circuits from their panels. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalCircuits.
- **ModifyElectricalCircuits** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the description, voltage, wiring type and used phases of electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalCircuitsData.
- **ModifyElectricalDevices** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the apparent power, load classification and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size) of electrical devices. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: electricalDevicesData.
- **ConnectToElectricalCircuits** (since 1.7.2): Connects electrical devices, or panels as sub-panels, to electrical circuits. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: connectionsData.
- **ModifyElectricalProjectSettings** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the electrical project settings: sets the default voltage and clears, adds or removes wiring types and load classifications. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: voltage, clearWiringTypes, clearLoadClassifications, wiringTypesToAdd, wiringTypesToRemove, loadClassificationsToAdd, loadClassificationsToRemove.
- **GetMEPElementDetails** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the type-specific details of the given MEP elements: insulation thickness and routing segment of rigid segments, control points of flexible segments, radius factor, insulation thickness, preference table and routing node of elbows (from Archicad 29), angle, length and insulation thickness of branches, and offsets, wider and narrower ports, insulation thickness, routing node and (from Archicad 29) preference table of transitions. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.

## MEP Commands (extended)

- **GetMEPPreferenceTableRows** (since 1.8.0): Gets rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle): whether the row is valid and its values (diameters, wall thickness, radius, length, angle, branch offset, connection length, description), and whether the table exists. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables only give whether they exist, as their rows have no key. On Archicad 27, which has one kind of preference table, a row is found by its shape and index and has a value and a description; the table's name and number of rows per shape are returned too. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: tableId, keys.
- **SetMEPPreferenceTableRows** (since 1.8.0): Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: tableId, rows.
- **AddMEPPreferenceTableRows** (since 1.8.0): Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: tableId, rows.
- **DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows** (since 1.8.0): Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: tableId, keys.
- **GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers** (since 1.8.0): Lists the preference tables of the Piping, Ventilation and Cable Carrier preference table containers of Archicad 27: their id, name, whether they exist and their number of rows per shape, and whether the container exists. Only for Archicad 27; from Archicad 28 use GetMEPPreferenceTables. Parameters: domains.
- **CreateMEPPreferenceTables** (since 1.8.0): Adds empty preference tables with the given names to the preference table container of a domain of Archicad 27 and returns their id, in one undo step. Only for Archicad 27. Parameters: domain, tables.

## Analytical Commands

- **GetCurrentAnalyticalModel** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the Structural Analytical Model created for the current view. Available from Archicad 27.
- **UpdateAnalyticalModel** (since 1.7.3): Triggers an update of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: analyticalModelId.
- **SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule** (since 1.7.3): Sets the generation settings of the current Structural Analytical Model to no rules. Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetAnalyticalModelCheckTypeId** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the type identifier of the Structural Analytical Model check. Available from Archicad 29.
- **GetAnalyticalModelVariation** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the variation of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given (the model is required before Archicad 27). The fields of the variation depend on the Archicad version. Parameters: analyticalModelId.
- **GetAnalyticalModel** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the Structural Analytical Model of the given variation, as returned by GetAnalyticalModelVariation. Parameters: variation.
- **GetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the visibility settings of the Structural Analytical Model. Available from Archicad 26.
- **SetAnalyticalVisibilitySettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the given fields of the Structural Analytical Model visibility settings; the others keep their value. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: visibilitySettings.
- **GetAnalyticalMemberTypesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the analytical member type (Beam, Column, Roof, Slab, Wall or Unknown) of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetAnalyticalLoadGroups** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the structural analysis load groups of the project with all their fields.
- **GetAnalyticalLoadCases** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the structural analysis load cases of the given load group, or of the project when no load group is given, with all their fields. Parameters: loadGroupId.
- **GetAnalyticalLoadCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the structural analysis load combinations of the project with all their fields and load factors.
- **CreateAnalyticalLoadGroups** (since 1.8.0): Creates structural analysis load groups in one undo step and returns their identifiers. Parameters: loadGroups.
- **CreateAnalyticalLoadCases** (since 1.8.0): Creates structural analysis load cases in the given load groups in one undo step and returns their identifiers. Parameters: loadCases.
- **CreateAnalyticalLoadCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Creates structural analysis load combinations, optionally with their load factors, in one undo step and returns their identifiers. The combination type is available from Archicad 27. Parameters: loadCombinations.
- **DeleteAnalyticalLoadGroups** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the given structural analysis load groups in one undo step. Parameters: loadGroupIds.
- **DeleteAnalyticalLoadCases** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the given structural analysis load cases in one undo step. Parameters: loadCaseIds.
- **DeleteAnalyticalLoadCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the given structural analysis load combinations in one undo step. Parameters: loadCombinationIds.
- **AddLoadCasesToLoadCombination** (since 1.8.0): Adds load cases with their factors to the given structural analysis load combination in one undo step. Parameters: loadCombinationId, loadFactors.
- **GetAnalyticalMembers** (since 1.8.0): Lists the elements of the curve and surface members of the given Structural Analytical Model, or of the model of the current view when no model is given (the model is required before Archicad 27). Parameters: analyticalModelId.
- **GetAnalyticalMemberDetails** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the curve, surface or segmented surface member of the given elements in a Structural Analytical Model, with their connections. Cross sections, curves, nodes and surfaces are returned with every field the Archicad version has. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements, segmentationCentralAngle.
- **GetAnalyticalReleases** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the releases of the given analytical members. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements.
- **SetAnalyticalReleases** (since 1.8.0): Replaces the releases of the given analytical members, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: releases.
- **GetCustomCurveMemberStretch** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the lengths added to the start and end of the given curve members. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetCustomCurveMemberStretch** (since 1.8.0): Sets the lengths added to the start and end of the given curve members, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: stretches.
- **GetLCSOfAnalyticalMembers** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the local coordinate system of the given analytical member parts, optionally in their intersection with another member part. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: memberParts.
- **GetAnalyticalMemberPartGeometries** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the node of the given analytical member vertices and the curve of the given member edges. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, memberPartRefs.
- **GetAnalyticalSupports** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the settings, the supported member part and the geometry of the given analytical supports. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements.
- **GetAnalyticalLinks** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the settings, the connected member parts and the geometry of the given analytical links. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements.
- **CreateAnalyticalSupports** (since 1.8.0): Creates analytical supports from their settings and supported member part, as GetAnalyticalSupports returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: supports.
- **CreateAnalyticalLinks** (since 1.8.0): Creates analytical links from their settings and connected member parts, as GetAnalyticalLinks returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: links.
- **ConvertAnalyticalLinksToNonShortest** (since 1.8.0): Converts the given shortest analytical links (associative to a curve member or a surface member edge) to links connected to a fixed coordinate, in one undo step, and returns the converted links. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements.
- **GetAnalyticalLoads** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the settings, the loaded member part, the custom data (the curve of an edge load, the contour of a surface load) and the geometry of the given analytical point, edge and surface loads. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: analyticalModelId, elements.
- **CreateAnalyticalLoads** (since 1.8.0): Creates analytical point, edge and surface loads from their settings, loaded member part and custom data, as GetAnalyticalLoads returns them, in one undo step. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: loads.

## Solid Element Operation Commands

- **CreateSolidElementLinks** (since 1.5.4): Creates solid element operation links between target and operator elements. Parameters: solidLinks.
- **RemoveSolidElementLinks** (since 1.5.4): Removes solid element operation links between target and operator elements. Parameters: solidLinks.
- **GetSolidElementLinks** (since 1.5.4): Returns solid element operation links for each queried element, grouped by role (target or operator). Parameters: elements.
- **CreateSolidOperations** (since 1.8.0): Runs a solid operation (subtraction, intersection, addition) on two morphs and returns the resulting morphs, one item per operation. Unlike CreateSolidElementLinks this is not a link: the target and the operator morph are replaced by the result. Morphs only; the operations run in one undo step. Parameters: operations.
- **TrimElements** (since 1.5.9): Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type. Parameters: elements, trimmingElement, trimType.
- **RemoveElementTrims** (since 1.5.9): Removes the trim between an element and the roof or shell trimming it. Parameters: elementPairs.
- **GetElementTrims** (since 1.5.9): Which roofs and shells trim each queried element, with the trim type, and which elements it trims. Parameters: elements.
- **MergeElements** (since 1.8.0): Merges the given construction elements (the Merge command of Archicad, which cleans up the junctions of slabs, beams, walls and similar elements). Undoable. The element types are not filtered: Archicad reports the ones it cannot merge. Parameters: elements.
- **UnmergeElements** (since 1.8.0): Removes the merge between the two elements of each given pair. Undoable; one execution result per pair. Parameters: elementPairs.
- **GetMergedElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the elements each queried element is merged with, one item per queried element; an unknown element is an error item. Parameters: elements.

## Script UI Commands

- **ShowScriptUI** (since 1.5.4): Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts). Parameters: htmlContent, width, height, title, resizable, zoomEnabled, zoomLevel, scrollBarsVisible, contextMenuEnabled, navigationDisabled, allowSelfSignedCertificates, clearCookies, autoHeight.
- **GetScriptUIResult** (since 1.5.4): Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from the Script UI palette's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the palette is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it.

## Developer Commands

- **GenerateDocumentation** (since 1.0.7): Generates files for the documentation. Used by Tapir developers only. Parameters: destinationFolder.
